Includes correspondence school, industrial, and commercial instructors; and adult education teachers and instructors who prepare persons to operate industrial machinery and equipment and transportation and communications equipment. Teaching may take place in public or private schools whose primary business is education or in a school associated with an organization whose primary business is other than education.
All postsecondary teachers not listed separately.

Occupation Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: This category includes teachers who work in various educational settings, such as preschools, elementary schools, middle schools, high schools, and special education programs. They provide instruction, create lesson plans, assess student progress, and support the overall development and well-being of students.

Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Teach young children basic skills and concepts to prepare them for primary school, focusing on social, motor, language, and foundational academic development.

Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Instruct preschool-aged children in activities designed to promote social, physical, and intellectual growth needed for primary school in preschool, day care center, or other child development facility. May be required to hold State certification.

Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Teach elemental natural and social science, personal hygiene, music, art, and literature to kindergarten students. Promote physical, mental, and social development. May be required to hold State certification.

Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Instruct students in multiple academic and developmental areas, typically from first through eighth grade, fostering foundational skills and knowledge.

Occupation Name: Elementary School Teachers, Except Special Education
Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Teach students basic academic, social, and other formative skills in public or private schools at the elementary level.

Occupation Name: Middle School Teachers, Except Special and Career/Technical Education
Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Teach students in one or more subjects in public or private schools at the middle, intermediate, or junior high level, which falls between elementary and senior high school as defined by applicable laws and regulations.

Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Teach occupational, career and technical, or vocational subjects in public or private schools at the middle, intermediate, or junior high level, which falls between elementary and senior high school as defined by applicable laws and regulations.

Minor Name: Preschool, Primary, Secondary, and Special Education School Teachers
Description: Teach one or more subjects to high school students, preparing them for postsecondary education, careers, or vocational training.

Teach or instruct courses other than those that normally lead to an occupational objective or degree. Courses may include self-improvement, nonvocational, and nonacademic subjects. Teaching may or may not take place in a traditional educational institution.

Occupation Name: Part-time Teachers and Instructors, All Other
Description: The 25-3030.00 series is essentially the umbrella for teaching roles that don’t neatly fit into the more traditional, permanent classroom positions. In this case, it specifically covers substitute teachers—those nimble educators who jump in on short notice to keep the learning train chugging along when regular teachers are absent. These professionals typically follow the established lesson plans to maintain continuity for students, ensuring that the educational process doesn’t miss a beat. So, in a nutshell, the 25-3030.00 series is all about keeping classrooms in session with the dynamic, adaptable talent of short-term substitute teachers!

Broad Name: Part-time Teachers and Instructors, All Other
Description: Teach students on a short-term basis as a temporary replacement for a regular classroom teacher, typically using the regular teacher's lesson plan.

Teacher Assistants, often known as paraprofessionals. These essential classroom allies support teachers by helping with instructional tasks, managing classroom activities, and offering individualized attention to students who might need a little extra help. Whether it's preparing learning materials, supervising small groups, or assisting in special education settings, teacher assistants play a key role in creating a nurturing and effective learning environment. If you enjoy working closely with students, thrive in a collaborative setting, and have a passion for making education accessible and engaging, this might be the perfect role for you—think of it as being the secret ingredient in the recipe for classroom success!
Instruct individual students or small groups of students in academic subjects to support formal class instruction or to prepare students for standardized or admissions tests.
Teach or instruct in specialized subjects not outlined under standard categories, potentially including private tutoring or specialty workshops.
All teachers and instructors not listed separately.
Provide non-classroom, academic instruction to students on an individual or small-group basis for proactive or remedial purposes.

This category includes professionals who work in libraries, museums, archives, and similar institutions. Librarians manage library collections, assist patrons in accessing information, and provide research support. Curators oversee collections in museums and galleries, organize exhibitions, and conduct research. Archivists preserve and maintain records and historical documents.
Appraise, preserve, and catalog historical documents, artwork, and museum collections. Organize exhibitions, conduct research, and maintain public or academic archives.
Appraise, edit, and direct safekeeping of permanent records and historically valuable documents. Participate in research activities based on archival materials.

Administer collections, such as artwork, collectibles, historic items, or scientific specimens of museums or other institutions. May conduct instructional, research, or public service activities of institution.

Restore, maintain, or prepare objects in museum collections for storage, research, or exhibit. May work with specimens such as fossils, skeletal parts, or botanicals; or artifacts, textiles, or art. May identify and record objects or install and arrange them in exhibits. Includes book or document conservators.
Manage library services, organize collections of books and digital media, assist patrons with research, and develop programs to encourage literacy and learning.

Administer libraries and perform related library services. Work in a variety of settings, including public libraries, educational institutions, museums, corporations, government agencies, law firms, non-profit organizations, and healthcare providers. Tasks may include selecting, acquiring, cataloguing, classifying, circulating, and maintaining library materials; and furnishing reference, bibliographical, and readers' advisory services. May perform in-depth, strategic research, and synthesize, analyze, edit, and filter information. May set up or work with databases and information systems to catalogue and access information.

Administer and maintain libraries or collections of information, for public or private access through reference or borrowing. Work in a variety of settings, such as educational institutions, museums, and corporations, and with various types of informational materials, such as books, periodicals, recordings, films, and databases. Tasks may include acquiring, cataloging, and circulating library materials, and user services such as locating and organizing information, providing instruction on how to access information, and setting up and operating a library's media equipment.
Support librarians by organizing materials, assisting with circulation, maintaining records, and helping users locate information.

Assist librarians by helping readers in the use of library catalogs, databases, and indexes to locate books and other materials; and by answering questions that require only brief consultation of standard reference. Compile records; sort and shelve books or other media; remove or repair damaged books or other media; register patrons; and check materials in and out of the circulation process. Replace materials in shelving area (stacks) or files. Includes bookmobile drivers who assist with providing services in mobile libraries.

These professionals provide support, assistance, and services in educational and library settings.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations
Description: Advise and educate individuals or families on agriculture, horticulture, nutrition, and home management techniques to improve efficiency, health, and sustainability.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations

Demonstrate procedures and apply research findings to solve problems; and instruct and train in product development, sales, and the use of machinery and equipment to promote general welfare. Includes county agricultural agents, feed and farm management advisors, home economists, and extension service advisors.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations
Description: Develop educational materials, coordinate curriculum standards, and provide training for teachers. Assess program effectiveness to enhance learning outcomes.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations
Description: Develop instructional material, coordinate educational content, and incorporate current technology in specialized fields that provide guidelines to educators and instructors for developing curricula and conducting courses. Includes educational consultants and specialists, and instructional material directors.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations
Description: Develop instructional materials and products and assist in the technology-based redesign of courses. Assist faculty in learning about, becoming proficient in, and applying instructional technology.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations
Description: Assist classroom teachers by providing additional support to students, preparing materials, and supervising classroom activities.

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations

Minor Name: Other Education, Training, and Library Occupations

Description: All education, training, and library workers not listed separately.

Assess, treat, and care for patients by manipulation of spine and musculoskeletal system. May provide spinal adjustment or address sacral or pelvic misalignment.
Diagnose and treat diseases, injuries, and malformations of the teeth and gums. Provide preventive care, perform dental surgeries, and educate patients on oral health.

Examine, diagnose, and treat diseases, injuries, and malformations of teeth and gums. May treat diseases of nerve, pulp, and other dental tissues affecting oral hygiene and retention of teeth. May fit dental appliances or provide preventive care.

Perform surgery and related procedures on the hard and soft tissues of the oral and maxillofacial regions to treat diseases, injuries, or defects. May diagnose problems of the oral and maxillofacial regions. May perform surgery to improve function or appearance.

Examine, diagnose, and treat dental malocclusions and oral cavity anomalies. Design and fabricate appliances to realign teeth and jaws to produce and maintain normal function and to improve appearance.

Construct oral prostheses to replace missing teeth and other oral structures to correct natural and acquired deformation of mouth and jaws, to restore and maintain oral function, such as chewing and speaking, and to improve appearance.
All dentists not listed separately.
Advise individuals or groups on nutritional practices to maintain or improve health. May plan and implement meal programs, assess dietary needs, and promote healthy eating.

Plan and conduct food service or nutritional programs to assist in the promotion of health and control of disease. May supervise activities of a department providing quantity food services, counsel individuals, or conduct nutritional research.
Examine eyes and visual systems, diagnose eye-related conditions, and prescribe lenses or other treatments to improve and protect vision.

Diagnose, manage, and treat conditions and diseases of the human eye and visual system. Examine eyes and visual system, diagnose problems or impairments, prescribe corrective lenses, and provide treatment. May prescribe therapeutic drugs to treat specific eye conditions.
Dispense prescription medications, provide expertise in drug therapy, and counsel patients on medication usage, side effects, and interactions.

Dispense drugs prescribed by physicians and other health practitioners and provide information to patients about medications and their use. May advise physicians and other health practitioners on the selection, dosage, interactions, and side effects of medications.
Diagnose illnesses, prescribe treatments, and perform procedures or surgeries to restore patient health. May specialize in areas like cardiology, pediatrics, or surgery.
Physicians who administer anesthetics prior to, during, or after surgery or other medical procedures.
Physicians who diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and injuries that commonly occur in the general population. May refer patients to specialists when needed for further diagnosis or treatment.

Physicians who diagnose and provide non-surgical treatment of diseases and injuries of internal organ systems. Provide care mainly for adults who have a wide range of problems associated with the internal organs.

Physicians who provide medical care related to pregnancy or childbirth and those who diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases of women, particularly those affecting the reproductive system. May also provide general medical care to women.
Physicians who diagnose, treat, and help prevent children's diseases and injuries.
Physicians who diagnose, treat, and help prevent disorders of the mind.
Physicians who treat diseases, injuries, and deformities by invasive, minimally-invasive, or non-invasive surgical methods, such as using instruments, appliances, or by manual manipulation.
All physicians and surgeons not listed separately.
Diagnose, treat, and help prevent allergic diseases and disease processes affecting the immune system.
Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases or other conditions of the skin.

Provide inpatient care predominantly in settings such as medical wards, acute care units, intensive care units, rehabilitation centers, or emergency rooms. Manage and coordinate patient care throughout treatment.
Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and disorders of the nervous system.
Diagnose and treat diseases using radioactive materials and techniques. May monitor radionuclide preparation, administration, and disposition.
Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases and injuries of the eyes and related structures.
Diagnose presence and stage of diseases using laboratory techniques and patient specimens. Study the nature, cause, and development of diseases. May perform autopsies.
Diagnose and treat disorders requiring physiotherapy to provide physical, mental, and occupational rehabilitation.

Apply knowledge of general preventive medicine and public health issues to promote health care to groups or individuals, and aid in the prevention or reduction of risk of disease, injury, disability, or death. May practice population-based medicine or diagnose and treat patients in the context of clinical health promotion and disease prevention.
Examine and diagnose disorders and diseases using x-rays and radioactive materials. May treat patients.
Diagnose, treat, and help prevent injuries that occur during sporting events, athletic training, and physical activities.
Diagnose, treat, and help prevent benign and malignant medical and surgical disorders of the genitourinary system and the renal glands.
Practice medicine under the supervision of physicians. Conduct examinations, diagnose conditions, provide treatment, and write prescriptions where legally permitted.

Provide healthcare services typically performed by a physician, under the supervision of a physician. Conduct complete physicals, provide treatment, and counsel patients. May, in some cases, prescribe medication. Must graduate from an accredited educational program for physician assistants.
Assist anesthesiologists in the administration of anesthesia for surgical and non-surgical procedures. Monitor patient status and provide patient care during surgical treatment.
Diagnose and treat diseases, deformities, and injuries of the foot, ankle, and lower leg. May perform surgeries, prescribe orthotics, or provide preventive care.
Diagnose and treat diseases and deformities of the human foot.
Provide rehabilitative, therapeutic services (e.g., physical, occupational, speech) to help patients overcome physical, mental, or developmental challenges.

Assess, plan, organize, and participate in rehabilitative programs that help build or restore vocational, homemaking, and daily living skills, as well as general independence, to persons with disabilities or developmental delays.

Occupation Name: Low Vision Therapists, Orientation and Mobility Specialists, and Vision Rehabilitation Therapists
Description: Provide therapy to patients with visual impairments to improve their functioning in daily life activities. May train patients in activities such as computer use, communication skills, or home management skills.

Assess, plan, organize, and participate in rehabilitative programs that improve mobility, relieve pain, increase strength, and improve or correct disabling conditions resulting from disease or injury.

Provide radiation therapy to patients as prescribed by a radiologist according to established practices and standards. Duties may include reviewing prescription and diagnosis; acting as liaison with physician and supportive care personnel; preparing equipment, such as immobilization, treatment, and protection devices; and maintaining records, reports, and files. May assist in dosimetry procedures and tumor localization.

Plan, direct, or coordinate medically-approved recreation programs for patients in hospitals, nursing homes, or other institutions. Activities include sports, trips, dramatics, social activities, and arts and crafts. May assess a patient condition and recommend appropriate recreational activity.
Plan or conduct art therapy sessions or programs to improve clients' physical, cognitive, or emotional well-being.
Plan, organize, or direct medically prescribed music therapy activities designed to positively influence patients' psychological or behavioral status.

Assess, treat, and care for patients with breathing disorders. Assume primary responsibility for all respiratory care modalities, including the supervision of respiratory therapy technicians. Initiate and conduct therapeutic procedures; maintain patient records; and select, assemble, check, and operate equipment.

Assess and treat persons with speech, language, voice, and fluency disorders. May select alternative communication systems and teach their use. May perform research related to speech and language problems.

Assess, plan, or implement fitness programs that include exercise or physical activities such as those designed to improve cardiorespiratory function, body composition, muscular strength, muscular endurance, or flexibility.
All therapists not listed separately.
Diagnose and treat diseases and injuries in animals. May perform surgeries, vaccinate animals, prescribe medications, and advise on care and feeding.
Diagnose, treat, or research diseases and injuries of animals. Includes veterinarians who conduct research and development, inspect livestock, or care for pets and companion animals.
Assess patients’ health problems, administer nursing care, educate patients and the public about health conditions, and maintain medical records.

Assess patient health problems and needs, develop and implement nursing care plans, and maintain medical records. Administer nursing care to ill, injured, convalescent, or disabled patients. May advise patients on health maintenance and disease prevention or provide case management. Licensing or registration required.

Provide advanced nursing care for patients with acute conditions such as heart attacks, respiratory distress syndrome, or shock. May care for pre- and post-operative patients or perform advanced, invasive diagnostic or therapeutic procedures.
Provide advanced nursing care for patients with psychiatric disorders. May provide psychotherapy under the direction of a psychiatrist.
Provide advanced nursing care for patients in critical or coronary care units.
Plan, direct, or coordinate the daily patient care activities in a clinical practice. Ensure adherence to established clinical policies, protocols, regulations, and standards.
Administer anesthesia, monitor patients’ vital signs, and oversee patient recovery from anesthesia under the guidance of anesthesiologists or other physicians.

Administer anesthesia, monitor patient's vital signs, and oversee patient recovery from anesthesia. May assist anesthesiologists, surgeons, other physicians, or dentists. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.
Provide prenatal, childbirth, and postpartum care to women, manage low-risk pregnancies, and offer reproductive health education and counseling.

Diagnose and coordinate all aspects of the birthing process, either independently or as part of a healthcare team. May provide well-woman gynecological care. Must have specialized, graduate nursing education.
Deliver advanced nursing services, including diagnosing and managing most common and chronic illnesses. Often focus on health promotion, disease prevention, and patient education.

Diagnose and treat acute, episodic, or chronic illness, independently or as part of a healthcare team. May focus on health promotion and disease prevention. May order, perform, or interpret diagnostic tests such as lab work and x rays. May prescribe medication. Must be registered nurses who have specialized graduate education.
Identify, assess, and manage disorders of hearing, balance, and related ear problems. May fit hearing aids and counsel patients on hearing loss adaptation.
Assess and treat persons with hearing and related disorders. May fit hearing aids and provide auditory training. May perform research related to hearing problems.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
Description: Occupations providing health assessment and treatment services not classified under a specific healthcare role, potentially including naturopaths, acupuncturists, or other specialized practitioners.

Occupation Name: Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners, All Other
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
Description: All health diagnosing and treating practitioners not listed separately.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
Description: Provide treatment of symptoms and disorders using needles and small electrical currents. May provide massage treatment. May also provide preventive treatments.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
Description: Diagnose, treat, and help prevent diseases using a system of practice that is based on the natural healing capacity of individuals. May use physiological, psychological or mechanical methods. May also use natural medicines, prescription or legend drugs, foods, herbs, or other natural remedies.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Diagnosing and Treating Practitioners
Description: Diagnose and treat visual system disorders such as binocular vision and eye movement impairments.

This category includes healthcare professionals who perform various technical and diagnostic procedures to support patient care. It encompasses occupations such as medical and clinical laboratory technologists, radiologic technologists, cardiovascular technologists, surgical technologists, and medical records and health information technicians. These professionals work in hospitals, clinics, diagnostic laboratories, and other healthcare settings.
Perform complex medical laboratory tests for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. Analyze blood, tissue, and body fluids.
Perform complex medical laboratory tests for diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. May train or supervise staff.
Analyze chromosomes found in biological specimens such as amniotic fluids, bone marrow, and blood to aid in the study, diagnosis, or treatment of genetic diseases.
Stain, mount, and study cells to detect evidence of cancer, hormonal abnormalities, and other pathological conditions following established standards and practices.
Prepare histologic slides from tissue sections for microscopic examination and diagnosis by pathologists. May assist in research studies.
Perform routine medical laboratory tests for the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of disease. May work under the supervision of a medical technologist.
Clean teeth, examine patients for signs of oral disease, and provide preventative dental care. May educate patients on ways to improve oral health.
Clean teeth and examine oral areas, head, and neck for signs of oral disease. May educate patients on oral hygiene, take and develop x rays, or apply fluoride or sealants.
Operate specialized diagnostic imaging equipment (e.g., X-rays, MRI) or perform tests to help healthcare providers diagnose diseases or injuries.

Conduct tests on pulmonary or cardiovascular systems of patients for diagnostic purposes. May conduct or assist in electrocardiograms, cardiac catheterizations, pulmonary functions, lung capacity, and similar tests. Includes vascular technologists.
Produce ultrasonic recordings of internal organs for use by physicians.

Prepare, administer, and measure radioactive isotopes in therapeutic, diagnostic, and tracer studies using a variety of radioisotope equipment. Prepare stock solutions of radioactive materials and calculate doses to be administered by radiologists. Subject patients to radiation. Execute blood volume, red cell survival, and fat absorption studies following standard laboratory techniques.
Take x rays and CAT scans or administer nonradioactive materials into patient's blood stream for diagnostic purposes. Includes technologists who specialize in other scanning modalities.

Operate Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scanners. Monitor patient safety and comfort, and view images of area being scanned to ensure quality of pictures. May administer gadolinium contrast dosage intravenously. May interview patient, explain MRI procedures, and position patient on examining table. May enter into the computer data such as patient history, anatomical area to be scanned, orientation specified, and position of entry.
Provide first-response medical care and transport for sick or injured individuals in emergency situations. Assess patient conditions, perform basic interventions, and communicate with hospital staff.
Assess injuries, administer emergency medical care, and extricate trapped individuals. Transport injured or sick persons to medical facilities.

Occupation Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Assist practitioners in fields like surgery, pharmacy, or rehabilitation by preparing equipment, handling specimens, or aiding in procedures.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Assist in the provision of food service and nutritional programs, under the supervision of a dietitian. May plan and produce meals based on established guidelines, teach principles of food and nutrition, or counsel individuals.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Prepare medications under the direction of a pharmacist. May measure, mix, count out, label, and record amounts and dosages of medications according to prescription orders.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Care for individuals with mental or emotional conditions or disabilities, following the instructions of physicians or other health practitioners. Monitor patients' physical and emotional well-being and report to medical staff. May participate in rehabilitation and treatment programs, help with personal hygiene, and administer oral or injectable medications.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Provide respiratory care under the direction of respiratory therapists and physicians.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Assist in operations, under the supervision of surgeons, registered nurses, or other surgical personnel. May help set up operating room, prepare and transport patients for surgery, adjust lights and equipment, pass instruments and other supplies to surgeons and surgeon's assistants, hold retractors, cut sutures, and help count sponges, needles, supplies, and instruments.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Perform medical tests in a laboratory environment for use in the treatment and diagnosis of diseases in animals. Prepare vaccines and serums for prevention of diseases. Prepare tissue samples, take blood samples, and execute laboratory tests, such as urinalysis and blood counts. Clean and sterilize instruments and materials and maintain equipment and machines. May assist a veterinarian during surgery.

Broad Name: Health Practitioner Support Technologists and Technicians
Description: Assist ophthalmologists by performing ophthalmic clinical functions. May administer eye exams, administer eye medications, and instruct the patient in care and use of corrective lenses.

Occupation Name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
Description: Provide basic nursing care under the direction of registered nurses and doctors. Monitor patients’ health, administer basic treatments, and keep records.

Occupation Name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
Broad Name: Licensed Practical and Licensed Vocational Nurses
Description: Care for ill, injured, or convalescing patients or persons with disabilities in hospitals, nursing homes, clinics, private homes, group homes, and similar institutions. May work under the supervision of a registered nurse. Licensing required.

Occupation Name: Medical Records and Health Information Technicians
Description: Organize and manage health information data, ensuring accuracy, accessibility, and security in both paper and electronic systems.

Occupation Name: Medical Records and Health Information Technicians
Broad Name: Medical Records and Health Information Technicians
Description: Compile, process, and maintain medical records of hospital and clinic patients in a manner consistent with medical, administrative, ethical, legal, and regulatory requirements of the health care system. Process, maintain, compile, and report patient information for health requirements and standards in a manner consistent with the healthcare industry's numerical coding system.
Fit and adjust eyeglasses or contact lenses according to prescriptions from ophthalmologists or optometrists. Help customers select frames and educate on lens care.

Design, measure, fit, and adapt lenses and frames for client according to written optical prescription or specification. Assist client with inserting, removing, and caring for contact lenses. Assist client with selecting frames. Measure customer for size of eyeglasses and coordinate frames with facial and eye measurements and optical prescription. Prepare work order for optical laboratory containing instructions for grinding and mounting lenses in frames. Verify exactness of finished lens spectacles. Adjust frame and lens position to fit client. May shape or reshape frames. Includes contact lens opticians.
Support healthcare delivery by performing specialized technical tasks not covered by other defined roles, such as surgical technologists or neurodiagnostic technologists.
Design, measure, fit, and adapt orthopedic braces, appliances or prostheses, such as limbs or facial parts for patients with disabling conditions.
Select and fit hearing aids for customers. Administer and interpret tests of hearing. Assess hearing instrument efficacy. Take ear impressions and prepare, design, and modify ear molds.

Occupation Name: Health Technologists and Technicians, All Other
Description: All health technologists and technicians not listed separately.
Conduct electroneurodiagnostic (END) tests such as electroencephalograms, evoked potentials, polysomnograms, or electronystagmograms. May perform nerve conduction studies.

Assist ophthalmologists by performing ophthalmic clinical functions and ophthalmic photography. Provide instruction and supervision to other ophthalmic personnel. Assist with minor surgical procedures, applying aseptic techniques and preparing instruments. May perform eye exams, administer eye medications, and instruct patients in care and use of corrective lenses.
Maintain and use equipment and supplies necessary to demonstrate portions of the human body on x-ray film or fluoroscopic screen for diagnostic purposes.

Assist surgeons during surgery by performing duties such as tissue retraction, insertion of tubes and intravenous lines, or closure of surgical wounds. Perform preoperative and postoperative duties to facilitate patient care.

Occupation Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Description: This category includes a diverse range of healthcare professionals who perform specialized roles in patient care, diagnostics, therapy, and technical support. It encompasses occupations such as dental hygienists, nuclear medicine technologists, veterinary technologists and technicians, ophthalmic medical technicians, and pharmacy technicians.

Occupation Name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists and Technicians
Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Description: Evaluate and analyze work environments to design programs and procedures that control, eliminate, and prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical, and biological agents.

Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Broad Name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists and Technicians
Description: Review, evaluate, and analyze work environments and design programs and procedures to control, eliminate, and prevent disease or injury caused by chemical, physical, and biological agents or ergonomic factors. May conduct inspections and enforce adherence to laws and regulations governing the health and safety of individuals. May be employed in the public or private sector. Includes environmental protection officers.

Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Broad Name: Occupational Health and Safety Specialists and Technicians
Description: Collect data on work environments for analysis by occupational health and safety specialists. Implement and conduct evaluation of programs designed to limit chemical, physical, biological, and ergonomic risks to workers.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous Health Practitioners and Technical Workers
Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Description: Engage in healthcare tasks not classified under other occupations. May involve emerging healthcare technologies or highly specialized medical support activities.

Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Practitioners and Technical Workers
Description: Evaluate and advise individuals to assist recovery from or avoid athletic-related injuries or illnesses, or maintain peak physical fitness. May provide first aid or emergency care.

Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Practitioners and Technical Workers
Description: Assess individual or family risk for a variety of inherited conditions, such as genetic disorders and birth defects. Provide information to other healthcare providers or to individuals and families concerned with the risk of inherited conditions. Advise individuals and families to support informed decisionmaking and coping methods for those at risk. May help conduct research related to genetic conditions or genetic counseling.

Occupation Name: Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Workers, All Other
Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Practitioners and Technical Workers
Description: All healthcare practitioners and technical workers not listed separately.

Minor Name: Other Healthcare Practitioners and Technical Occupations
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Health Practitioners and Technical Workers
Description: Provide prenatal care and childbirth assistance.

Provides assistance to healthcare practitioners, including aides and assistants who handle patient care tasks, administrative support, or routine clinical procedures under supervision of licensed professionals.

Occupation Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: This category includes healthcare professionals who provide essential care and assistance to patients in various settings. It encompasses occupations such as registered nurses, licensed practical and vocational nurses, psychiatric aides, home health aides, and personal care aides. These professionals work in hospitals, nursing homes, psychiatric facilities, home healthcare settings, and other healthcare institutions.

Occupation Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Minor Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: Provide basic patient care in home, long-term care, or hospital settings. Monitor vital signs, assist with daily living activities, and report patient status to nursing staff.

Minor Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Broad Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: Provide routine individualized healthcare such as changing bandages and dressing wounds, and applying topical medications to the elderly, convalescents, or persons with disabilities at the patient's home or in a care facility. Monitor or report changes in health status. May also provide personal care such as bathing, dressing, and grooming of patient.

Minor Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Broad Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: Provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. Perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, or move patients, or change linens. May transfer or transport patients. Includes nursing care attendants, nursing aides, and nursing attendants.

Minor Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Broad Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: Assist mentally impaired or emotionally disturbed patients, working under direction of nursing and medical staff. May assist with daily living activities, lead patients in educational and recreational activities, or accompany patients to and from examinations and treatments. May restrain violent patients. Includes psychiatric orderlies.

Minor Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Broad Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: Provide basic patient care under direction of nursing staff. Perform duties such as feed, bathe, dress, groom, or move patients, or change linens. May transfer or transport patients. Includes nursing care attendants, nursing aides, and nursing attendants.

Minor Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Broad Name: Nursing, Psychiatric, and Home Health Aides
Description: Transport patients to areas such as operating rooms or x-ray rooms using wheelchairs, stretchers, or moveable beds. May maintain stocks of supplies or clean and transport equipment.

Occupation Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: This category includes healthcare professionals who work under the guidance of occupational therapists and physical therapists to provide support and assistance to patients during therapy sessions. It encompasses occupations such as occupational therapy assistants, occupational therapy aides, physical therapist assistants, and physical therapist aides. These professionals assist patients in performing therapeutic exercises, prepare treatment areas, and provide support to therapists in delivering care.

Minor Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: Help occupational therapists provide rehabilitative services to patients, assisting in treatments designed to improve mobility, coordination, and daily living skills.

Minor Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: Assist occupational therapists in providing occupational therapy treatments and procedures. May, in accordance with State laws, assist in development of treatment plans, carry out routine functions, direct activity programs, and document the progress of treatments. Generally requires formal training.

Minor Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: Under close supervision of an occupational therapist or occupational therapy assistant, perform only delegated, selected, or routine tasks in specific situations. These duties include preparing patient and treatment room.

Minor Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: Assist physical therapists in providing treatments that improve patient mobility, relieve pain, and prevent or limit permanent physical disabilities.

Minor Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: Assist physical therapists in providing physical therapy treatments and procedures. May, in accordance with State laws, assist in the development of treatment plans, carry out routine functions, document the progress of treatment, and modify specific treatments in accordance with patient status and within the scope of treatment plans established by a physical therapist. Generally requires formal training.

Minor Name: Occupational Therapy and Physical Therapist Assistants and Aides
Description: Under close supervision of a physical therapist or physical therapy assistant, perform only delegated, selected, or routine tasks in specific situations. These duties include preparing the patient and the treatment area.

This category includes a variety of healthcare support roles that provide assistance and support to healthcare professionals and patients. It encompasses occupations such as medical transcriptionists, pharmacy aides, veterinary assistants and laboratory animal caretakers, dietetic technicians, and medical equipment preparers. These professionals work in hospitals, clinics, laboratories, pharmacies, and other healthcare settings.
Use touch to manipulate soft-tissue muscles of the body, relieving pain, improving circulation, or promoting relaxation. May also advise clients on stretching, strengthening, and overall wellness.
Perform therapeutic massages of soft tissues and joints. May assist in the assessment of range of motion and muscle strength, or propose client therapy plans.
Deliver allied health support services not classified under specific roles, including specialized therapeutic aides or other emerging support positions in healthcare settings.
Assist dentist, set up equipment, prepare patient for treatment, and keep records.

Perform administrative and certain clinical duties under the direction of a physician. Administrative duties may include scheduling appointments, maintaining medical records, billing, and coding information for insurance purposes. Clinical duties may include taking and recording vital signs and medical histories, preparing patients for examination, drawing blood, and administering medications as directed by physician.
Prepare, sterilize, install, or clean laboratory or healthcare equipment. May perform routine laboratory tasks and operate or inspect equipment.

Transcribe medical reports recorded by physicians and other healthcare practitioners using various electronic devices, covering office visits, emergency room visits, diagnostic imaging studies, operations, chart reviews, and final summaries. Transcribe dictated reports and translate abbreviations into fully understandable form. Edit as necessary and return reports in either printed or electronic form for review and signature, or correction.
Record drugs delivered to the pharmacy, store incoming merchandise, and inform the supervisor of stock needs. May operate cash register and accept prescriptions for filling.

Occupation Name: Veterinary Assistants and Laboratory Animal Caretakers
Description: Feed, water, and examine pets and other nonfarm animals for signs of illness, disease, or injury in laboratories and animal hospitals and clinics. Clean and disinfect cages and work areas, and sterilize laboratory and surgical equipment. May provide routine post-operative care, administer medication orally or topically, or prepare samples for laboratory examination under the supervision of veterinary or laboratory animal technologists or technicians, veterinarians, or scientists.
Draw blood for tests, transfusions, donations, or research. May explain the procedure to patients and assist in the recovery of patients with adverse reactions.
All healthcare support workers not listed separately.

Assist speech-language pathologists in the assessment and treatment of speech, language, voice, and fluency disorders. Implement speech and language programs or activities as planned and directed by speech-language pathologists. Monitor the use of alternative communication devices and systems.
Maintain a sterile field to provide support for physicians and nurses during endoscopy procedures. Prepare and maintain instruments and equipment. May obtain specimens.
Responsible for safeguarding people, property, and institutions. Occupations include law enforcement officers, firefighters, corrections staff, and other roles ensuring public safety.

This category includes supervisors who oversee and manage the activities of protective service workers in various industries. It encompasses occupations such as police supervisors, fire and emergency medical service supervisors, gaming supervisors, and transportation security screeners supervisors. These professionals ensure compliance with regulations, provide guidance to subordinates, and maintain the efficiency and effectiveness of protective service operations.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Law Enforcement Workers
Description: Direct and coordinate activities of police officers or other law enforcement personnel. Oversee training, patrol, investigations, and administrative tasks.

Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Law Enforcement Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of correctional officers and jailers.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Police and Detectives
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Law Enforcement Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of members of police force.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
Description: Supervise and coordinate firefighters or other staff responding to fires and other emergencies. Oversee rescue operations, equipment maintenance, and training.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in fire fighting and fire prevention and control.

Occupation Name: Municipal Fire Fighting and Prevention Supervisors
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
Description: Supervise fire fighters who control and extinguish municipal fires, protect life and property, and conduct rescue efforts.

Occupation Name: Forest Fire Fighting and Prevention Supervisors
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Fire Fighting and Prevention Workers
Description: Supervise fire fighters who control and suppress fires in forests or vacant public land.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous First-Line Supervisors, Protective Service Workers
Description: Provide oversight for protective service personnel not included in standard categories, such as lifeguard supervisors or security shift leaders.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Protective Service Workers, All Other
Broad Name: Miscellaneous First-Line Supervisors, Protective Service Workers
Description: All protective service supervisors not listed separately above.

This category includes professionals who specialize in fire prevention, fire suppression, and emergency response. It encompasses occupations such as firefighters, fire inspectors, and fire investigators. Firefighters respond to emergency situations, extinguish fires, and provide medical assistance. Fire inspectors ensure compliance with fire codes and regulations, while fire investigators determine the cause and origin of fires.
Combat and extinguish fires, respond to emergencies, and safeguard life and property. Perform rescue operations, administer first aid, and maintain firefighting equipment.

Control and extinguish fires or respond to emergency situations where life, property, or the environment is at risk. Duties may include fire prevention, emergency medical service, hazardous material response, search and rescue, and disaster assistance.
Control and extinguish municipal fires, protect life and property and conduct rescue efforts.
Control and suppress fires in forests or vacant public land.
Inspect buildings to detect fire hazards and enforce local ordinances or state laws regulating fire safety. Investigate fire causes and origins.
Inspect buildings to detect fire hazards and enforce local ordinances and State laws, or investigate and gather facts to determine cause of fires and explosions.
Inspect buildings and equipment to detect fire hazards and enforce state and local regulations.
Conduct investigations to determine causes of fires and explosions.

Occupation Name: Forest Fire Inspectors and Prevention Specialists
Description: Enforce fire regulations, inspect forest for fire hazards and recommend forest fire prevention or control measures. May report forest fires and weather conditions.

This category includes occupations such as police officers, detectives, and transit and railroad police. Law Enforcement Workers are responsible for maintaining public safety, enforcing laws, conducting investigations, and ensuring the security of individuals and property.
Maintain order in courts or supervise correctional facility inmates. Enforce rules, conduct searches, and ensure safety and security.
Maintain order in courts of law.

Guard inmates in penal or rehabilitative institutions in accordance with established regulations and procedures. May guard prisoners in transit between jail, courtroom, prison, or other point. Includes deputy sheriffs and police who spend the majority of their time guarding prisoners in correctional institutions.
Gather facts and collect evidence for criminal cases. Conduct interviews, surveillance, and investigations to solve crimes.
Conduct investigations related to suspected violations of Federal, State, or local laws to prevent or solve crimes.
Conduct investigations to prevent crimes or solve criminal cases.
Collect evidence at crime scene, classify and identify fingerprints, and photograph evidence for use in criminal and civil cases.
Investigate alleged or suspected criminal violations of Federal, state, or local laws to determine if evidence is sufficient to recommend prosecution.

Investigate and inspect persons, common carriers, goods, and merchandise, arriving in or departing from the United States or between states to detect violations of immigration and customs laws and regulations.

Gather, analyze, or evaluate information from a variety of sources, such as law enforcement databases, surveillance, intelligence networks or geographic information systems. Use intelligence data to anticipate and prevent organized crime activities, such as terrorism.
Enforce fishing, hunting, and boating laws. Patrol wildlife areas, investigate complaints, and ensure protection of wildlife populations.
Patrol assigned area to prevent fish and game law violations. Investigate reports of damage to crops or property by wildlife. Compile biological data.
Monitor parking regulations, issue tickets for violations, and direct vehicle or pedestrian traffic as needed.
Patrol assigned area, such as public parking lot or city streets to issue tickets to overtime parking violators and illegally parked vehicles.
Protect life and property, enforce laws, patrol assigned areas, respond to emergencies, and investigate crimes.

Maintain order and protect life and property by enforcing local, tribal, State, or Federal laws and ordinances. Perform a combination of the following duties: patrol a specific area; direct traffic; issue traffic summonses; investigate accidents; apprehend and arrest suspects, or serve legal processes of courts.
Patrol assigned area to enforce laws and ordinances, regulate traffic, control crowds, prevent crime, and arrest violators.
Enforce law and order in rural or unincorporated districts or serve legal processes of courts. May patrol courthouse, guard court or grand jury, or escort defendants.
Protect and police railroad and transit property, employees, or passengers.

This category includes occupations such as security guards, gaming surveillance officers, and transportation security screeners. Other Protective Service Workers are responsible for ensuring the safety and security of individuals, properties, and facilities in various settings.
Handle situations involving stray, dangerous, or abused animals. Enforce animal licensing laws and investigate reports of animal mistreatment.
Handle animals for the purpose of investigations of mistreatment, or control of abandoned, dangerous, or unattended animals.
Gather information for clients using interviews, surveillance, or research. May investigate financial, legal, or personal matters.
Gather, analyze, compile and report information regarding individuals or organizations to clients, or detect occurrences of unlawful acts or infractions of rules in private establishment.

Occupation Name: Security Guards and Gaming Surveillance Officers
Description: Guard property against theft, vandalism, or illegal activity. Monitor premises, check identification, and use video surveillance in casinos and other facilities.

Occupation Name: Gaming Surveillance Officers and Gaming Investigators
Broad Name: Security Guards and Gaming Surveillance Officers
Description: Act as oversight and security agent for management and customers. Observe casino or casino hotel operation for irregular activities such as cheating or theft by either employees or patrons. May use one-way mirrors above the casino floor, cashier's cage, and from desk. Use of audio/video equipment is also common to observe operation of the business. Usually required to provide verbal and written reports of all violations and suspicious behavior to supervisor.

Broad Name: Security Guards and Gaming Surveillance Officers
Description: Guard, patrol, or monitor premises to prevent theft, violence, or infractions of rules. May operate x-ray and metal detector equipment.
Engage in protective service roles not classified elsewhere, such as crossing guards, transportation security screeners, or school security.
Guide or control vehicular or pedestrian traffic at such places as streets, schools, railroad crossings, or construction sites.

Occupation Name: Lifeguards, Ski Patrol, and Other Recreational Protective Service Workers
Description: Monitor recreational areas, such as pools, beaches, or ski slopes to provide assistance and protection to participants.

Conduct screening of passengers, baggage, or cargo to ensure compliance with Transportation Security Administration (TSA) regulations. May operate basic security equipment such as x-ray machines and hand wands at screening checkpoints.
All protective service workers not listed separately.

Implement procedures and systems to prevent merchandise loss. Conduct audits and investigations of employee activity. May assist in developing policies, procedures, and systems for safeguarding assets.

Occupation Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Involves preparing and serving food and beverages in restaurants, cafeterias, and other dining establishments. Includes cooks, waitstaff, bartenders, and related support staff.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: This category includes supervisors and managers who oversee food preparation and serving workers in various establishments such as restaurants, cafeterias, and catering services. They are responsible for managing staff, ensuring food safety and quality, coordinating operations, and maintaining customer satisfaction.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Description: Direct and coordinate activities of workers engaged in preparing and serving food. Schedule shifts, ensure quality standards, and handle customer complaints.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Broad Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Description: Direct and may participate in the preparation, seasoning, and cooking of salads, soups, fish, meats, vegetables, desserts, or other foods. May plan and price menu items, order supplies, and keep records and accounts.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Broad Name: Supervisors of Food Preparation and Serving Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in preparing and serving food.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Cooks and Food Preparation Workers are responsible for preparing ingredients, cooking meals, following recipes, and ensuring food safety and quality. They work under the guidance of chefs, supervisors, or kitchen managers, and their tasks may include chopping vegetables, seasoning dishes, operating cooking equipment, and maintaining cleanliness in the kitchen area.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare meals according to recipes and customer requests in restaurants or other food establishments. Monitor food quality, safety, and sanitation.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare and cook food in a fast food restaurant with a limited menu. Duties of these cooks are limited to preparation of a few basic items and normally involve operating large-volume single-purpose cooking equipment.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare and cook large quantities of food for institutions, such as schools, hospitals, or cafeterias.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare meals in private homes. Includes personal chefs.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare, season, and cook dishes such as soups, meats, vegetables, or desserts in restaurants. May order supplies, keep records and accounts, price items on menu, or plan menu.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare and cook to order a variety of foods that require only a short preparation time. May take orders from customers and serve patrons at counters or tables.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: All cooks not listed separately.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Perform basic cooking tasks, such as chopping ingredients and preparing cold foods. Maintain kitchen cleanliness and adhere to food safety standards.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Perform a variety of food preparation duties other than cooking, such as preparing cold foods and shellfish, slicing meat, and brewing coffee or tea.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Food and Beverage Serving Workers encompass a range of positions in the food service industry, including waiters, waitresses, bartenders, hosts/hostesses, and counter attendants. They work in restaurants, bars, cafes, hotels, and other dining establishments. Their responsibilities include taking orders, serving food and beverages, ensuring customer satisfaction, and maintaining a clean and welcoming dining environment.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Mix and serve alcoholic and nonalcoholic beverages to patrons. May collect payments, manage bar inventory, and maintain cleanliness.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Mix and serve drinks to patrons, directly or through waitstaff.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Serve food and beverages, often at fast-food or self-service establishments. Take orders, process payments, and handle simple meal assembly.

Occupation Name: Combined Food Preparation and Serving Workers, Including Fast Food
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Perform duties which combine preparing and serving food and nonalcoholic beverages.

Occupation Name: Counter Attendants, Cafeteria, Food Concession, and Coffee Shop
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Serve food to diners at counter or from a steam table.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Prepare or serve specialty coffee or other beverages. Serve food such as baked goods or sandwiches to patrons.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Take orders and serve food and beverages to patrons. Provide menu information, address customer needs, and handle payments.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Take orders and serve food and beverages to patrons at tables in dining establishment.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Serve food at locations such as hospitals, hotels, and offices that do not operate as traditional restaurants.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Serve food to individuals outside of a restaurant environment, such as in hotel rooms, hospital rooms, residential care facilities, or cars.

Occupation Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Description: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers assist in the preparation and serving of food and beverages in various dining establishments such as restaurants, cafeterias, and fast food outlets. They may be responsible for tasks like clearing tables, restocking supplies, operating cash registers, and cleaning kitchen or dining areas.

Occupation Name: Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Description: Facilitate the dining experience by cleaning tables, restocking supplies, and supporting waitstaff or bartenders.

Occupation Name: Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Broad Name: Dining Room and Cafeteria Attendants and Bartender Helpers
Description: Facilitate food service. Clean tables, remove dirty dishes, replace soiled table linens; set tables; replenish supply of clean linens, silverware, glassware, and dishes; supply service bar with food; and serve items such as water, condiments, and coffee to patrons.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Description: Clean dishes, kitchen utensils, and work areas. May also store clean items in designated areas and remove trash.

Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Description: Clean dishes, kitchen, food preparation equipment, or utensils.

Occupation Name: Hosts and Hostesses, Restaurant, Lounge, and Coffee Shop
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Description: Greet guests, manage waitlists, guide patrons to their seats, and maintain an organized seating chart.

Occupation Name: Hosts and Hostesses, Restaurant, Lounge, and Coffee Shop
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Broad Name: Hosts and Hostesses, Restaurant, Lounge, and Coffee Shop
Description: Welcome patrons, seat them at tables or in lounge, and help ensure quality of facilities and service.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Description: Perform a variety of food service tasks not classified under other categories, such as delivering room service or assisting with catering events.

Occupation Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers, All Other
Major Name: Food Preparation and Serving Related Occupations
Minor Name: Other Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Food Preparation and Serving Related Workers
Description: All food preparation and serving related workers not listed separately.

Occupation Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Encompasses custodial and housekeeping roles maintaining interior and exterior spaces. Workers clean, repair, and manage areas such as offices, hotels, or grounds, ensuring a safe and sanitary environment.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers are responsible for coordinating and managing the work of cleaning and maintenance staff. They assign tasks, ensure compliance with safety standards, inspect work quality, and may handle administrative duties related to scheduling, budgeting, and inventory management.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Description: Oversee and coordinate janitorial or maintenance personnel. Schedule work shifts, inspect facilities, and ensure safety and cleanliness standards.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Housekeeping and Janitorial Workers
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate work activities of cleaning personnel in hotels, hospitals, offices, and other establishments.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Landscaping, Lawn Service, and Groundskeeping Workers
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of workers engaged in landscaping or groundskeeping activities. Work may involve reviewing contracts to ascertain service, machine, and workforce requirements; answering inquiries from potential customers regarding methods, material, and price ranges; and preparing estimates according to labor, material, and machine costs.

Occupation Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers perform tasks related to cleaning and maintaining buildings, such as janitorial work, custodial services, and pest control. Their responsibilities may include sweeping, mopping, vacuuming, waste removal, disinfecting surfaces, and implementing pest control measures.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Description: Clean buildings or private residences. Duties may include mopping, vacuuming, trash disposal, and sanitizing surfaces.

Occupation Name: Janitors and Cleaners, Except Maids and Housekeeping Cleaners
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Description: Keep buildings in clean and orderly condition. Perform heavy cleaning duties, such as cleaning floors, shampooing rugs, washing walls and glass, and removing rubbish. Duties may include tending furnace and boiler, performing routine maintenance activities, notifying management of need for repairs, and cleaning snow or debris from sidewalk.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Description: Perform any combination of light cleaning duties to maintain private households or commercial establishments, such as hotels and hospitals, in a clean and orderly manner. Duties may include making beds, replenishing linens, cleaning rooms and halls, and vacuuming.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Description: All building cleaning workers not listed separately.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Description: Identify and control pests using chemicals, traps, or natural solutions. Inspect buildings for infestation and recommend prevention measures.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Minor Name: Building Cleaning and Pest Control Workers
Description: Apply or release chemical solutions or toxic gases and set traps to kill or remove pests and vermin that infest buildings and surrounding areas.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Grounds Maintenance Workers perform tasks related to landscaping, lawn care, planting, pruning, irrigation, and maintenance of outdoor areas. They may also operate machinery and equipment, such as mowers, trimmers, and power tools.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Maintain outdoor areas, mow lawns, plant and trim vegetation, clear debris, and keep landscapes looking their best.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Landscape or maintain grounds of property using hand or power tools or equipment. Workers typically perform a variety of tasks, which may include any combination of the following: sod laying, mowing, trimming, planting, watering, fertilizing, digging, raking, sprinkler installation, and installation of mortarless segmental concrete masonry wall units.

Occupation Name: Pesticide Handlers, Sprayers, and Applicators, Vegetation
Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Mix or apply pesticides, herbicides, fungicides, or insecticides through sprays, dusts, vapors, soil incorporation, or chemical application on trees, shrubs, lawns, or botanical crops. Usually requires specific training and State or Federal certification.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: Using sophisticated climbing and rigging techniques, cut away dead or excess branches from trees or shrubs to maintain right-of-way for roads, sidewalks, or utilities, or to improve appearance, health, and value of tree. Prune or treat trees or shrubs using handsaws, hand pruners, clippers, and power pruners. Works off the ground in the tree canopy and may use truck-mounted lifts.

Major Name: Building and Grounds Cleaning and Maintenance Occupations
Description: All grounds maintenance workers not listed separately.
Provides personal services to clients, such as childcare, fitness instruction, or beauty treatments. Includes hairdressers, childcare workers, fitness trainers, and similar service providers.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Description: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers oversee and coordinate the activities of workers providing personal care services to individuals in various settings, such as home care, residential facilities, or healthcare institutions. They may supervise workers such as personal care aides, home health aides, and childcare workers, ensuring the quality of care and adherence to regulations.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of gaming service employees, such as dealers and slot supervisors. Ensure compliance with gaming regulations and maintain customer satisfaction.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Description: Supervise and coordinate activities of workers in assigned gaming areas. Circulate among tables and observe operations. Ensure that stations and games are covered for each shift. May explain and interpret operating rules of house to patrons. May plan and organize activities and services for guests in hotels/casinos. May address service complaints.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Description: Supervise and coordinate activities of slot department workers to provide service to patrons. Handle and settle complaints of players. Verify and pay off jackpots. Reset slot machines after payoffs. Make repairs or adjustments to slot machines or recommend removal of slot machines for repair. Report hazards and enforce safety rules.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Description: Direct workers providing personal services (e.g., spa, salon, or childcare). Monitor operations, train staff, and handle customer complaints or special requests.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of personal service workers, such as flight attendants, hairdressers, or caddies.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Personal Care and Service Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Personal Service Workers
Description: Plan, direct, or coordinate activities of a spa facility. Coordinate programs, schedule and direct staff, and oversee financial activities.

Animal Care and Service Workers provide care, support, and services to animals in a variety of settings, such as animal shelters, zoos, veterinary clinics, and pet care facilities. They may be involved in tasks such as feeding, grooming, training, monitoring health, and ensuring the overall well-being of animals.

Train animals for riding, harness, security, performance, or obedience, or assisting persons with disabilities. Accustom animals to human voice and contact; and condition animals to respond to commands. Train animals according to prescribed standards for show or competition. May train animals to carry pack loads or work as part of pack team.

Feed, water, groom, bathe, exercise, or otherwise care for pets and other nonfarm animals, such as dogs, cats, ornamental fish or birds, zoo animals, and mice. Work in settings such as kennels, animal shelters, zoos, circuses, and aquariums. May keep records of feedings, treatments, and animals received or discharged. May clean, disinfect, and repair cages, pens, or fish tanks.

This category includes various occupations involved in providing entertainment services and assisting with the operations of entertainment venues. It encompasses workers who support and facilitate the smooth running of events, performances, amusement parks, and other entertainment establishments.
Operate gambling tables, deal cards, or handle slot machines in casinos. Assist patrons, enforce gaming rules, and handle financial transactions.

Operate table games. Stand or sit behind table and operate games of chance by dispensing the appropriate number of cards or blocks to players, or operating other gaming equipment. Distribute winnings or collect players' money or chips. May compare the house's hand against players' hands.

Occupation Name: Gaming and Sports Book Writers and Runners
Description: Post information enabling patrons to wager on various races and sporting events. Assist in the operation of games such as keno and bingo. May operate random number generating equipment and announce the numbers for patrons. Receive, verify, and record patrons' wagers. Scan and process winning tickets presented by patrons and payout winnings for those wagers.
All gaming service workers not listed separately.
Operate film or digital projectors, manage reels or digital files, adjust sound and picture quality, and ensure smooth theatrical screenings.
Set up and operate motion picture projection and related sound reproduction equipment.

Occupation Name: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
Description: Greet patrons, take tickets, and direct attendees to seats. May distribute programs, answer questions, or help maintain order before and after events.

Occupation Name: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
Broad Name: Ushers, Lobby Attendants, and Ticket Takers
