Description: Exchange coins, tokens, and chips for patrons' money. May issue payoffs and obtain customer's signature on receipt. May operate a booth in the slot machine area and furnish change persons with money bank at the start of the shift, or count and audit money in drawers.

Occupation Name: Counter and Rental Clerks and Parts Salespersons
Description: Assist customers in finding products, including rentals or parts. Provide product information, manage transactions, and maintain stock.

Broad Name: Counter and Rental Clerks and Parts Salespersons
Description: Receive orders, generally in person, for repairs, rentals, and services. May describe available options, compute costs, and accept payment.

Broad Name: Counter and Rental Clerks and Parts Salespersons
Description: Sell spare and replacement parts and equipment in repair shop or parts store.
Sell merchandise such as clothing, furniture, or electronics. Greet customers, explain features, and ring up purchases.
Sell merchandise, such as furniture, motor vehicles, appliances, or apparel to consumers.

Sales Representatives, Services are professionals who are responsible for selling various services to businesses and individuals. They may work in industries such as advertising, financial services, consulting, and technology. These sales representatives build relationships with clients, identify their needs, and present suitable service solutions.
Sell or solicit advertising to businesses and individuals. Maintain client accounts, develop ad campaigns, and achieve sales targets.

Sell or solicit advertising space, time, or media in publications, signage, TV, radio, or the Internet. Includes individuals who obtain leases for outdoor advertising sites or persuade retailers to use sales promotion display items.
Contact potential clients, explain various insurance policies, and help customers choose plans that meet their needs.
Sell life, property, casualty, health, automotive, or other types of insurance. May refer clients to independent brokers, work as an independent broker, or be employed by an insurance company.

Occupation Name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
Description: Buy and sell stocks, bonds, or other financial instruments. Advise clients on investment strategies and market conditions.

Occupation Name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
Broad Name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
Description: Buy and sell securities or commodities in investment and trading firms, or provide financial services to businesses and individuals. May advise customers about stocks, bonds, mutual funds, commodities, and market conditions.

Broad Name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
Description: Buy and sell securities in investment and trading firms and develop and implement financial plans for individuals, businesses, and organizations.

Broad Name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
Description: Sell financial services, such as loan, tax, and securities counseling to customers of financial institutions and business establishments.

Broad Name: Securities, Commodities, and Financial Services Sales Agents
Description: Buy and sell securities and commodities to transfer debt, capital, or risk. Establish and negotiate unit prices and terms of sale.
Plan and sell transportation, lodging, and entertainment activities for clients. Offer advice on destinations, itineraries, and travel costs.

Plan and sell transportation and accommodations for travel agency customers. Determine destination, modes of transportation, travel dates, costs, and accommodations required. May also describe, plan, and arrange itineraries and sell tour packages. May assist in resolving clients' travel problems.
Sell services (e.g., digital marketing, consulting) not categorized under other sales roles. May create client proposals and follow up on leads.
All services sales representatives not listed separately.
Buy or sell energy products on the behalf of residential or commercial customers or utilities. Negotiate and oversee contracts for energy sales.

Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing are professionals who are responsible for selling goods and products to businesses (wholesale) or retailers (manufacturing). They work in various industries such as manufacturing, wholesale trade, and distribution. These sales representatives build relationships with clients, showcase product features, negotiate contracts, and close sales deals.
Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers to businesses, government agencies, or other organizations. Negotiate prices, explain product features, and maintain customer relationships.

Occupation Name: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Technical and Scientific Products
Description: Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers where technical or scientific knowledge is required in such areas as biology, engineering, chemistry, and electronics, normally obtained from at least 2 years of post-secondary education.
Contact new or existing customers to determine their solar equipment needs, suggest systems or equipment, or estimate costs.

Occupation Name: Sales Representatives, Wholesale and Manufacturing, Except Technical and Scientific Products
Description: Sell goods for wholesalers or manufacturers to businesses or groups of individuals. Work requires substantial knowledge of items sold.

Other Sales and Related Workers include a diverse range of occupations that are involved in sales and related activities, but are not classified under the specific subcategories within the sales occupation group. These occupations may include sales support roles, retail sales support, sales coordinators, sales assistants, and other sales-related positions.
Display and promote products at events or retail locations. Interact with customers, answer questions, and encourage product sales.
Demonstrate merchandise and answer questions for the purpose of creating public interest in buying the product. May sell demonstrated merchandise.

Model garments or other apparel and accessories for prospective buyers at fashion shows, private showings, or retail establishments. May pose for photos to be used in magazines or advertisements. May pose as subject for paintings, sculptures, and other types of artistic expression.

Occupation Name: Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents
Description: Assist clients in buying, selling, and renting properties. Conduct property showings, prepare contracts, and negotiate terms of sale or lease.

Broad Name: Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents
Description: Operate real estate office, or work for commercial real estate firm, overseeing real estate transactions. Other duties usually include selling real estate or renting properties and arranging loans.

Broad Name: Real Estate Brokers and Sales Agents
Description: Rent, buy, or sell property for clients. Perform duties, such as study property listings, interview prospective clients, accompany clients to property site, discuss conditions of sale, and draw up real estate contracts. Includes agents who represent buyer.
Sell complex scientific or technical products to businesses, leveraging engineering or technical knowledge to demonstrate product benefits and functionalities.
Sell business goods or services, the selling of which requires a technical background equivalent to a baccalaureate degree in engineering.
Solicit sales or donations over the phone. Follow scripts, answer questions, record customer details, and process payment information.
Solicit donations or orders for goods or services over the telephone.
Perform sales-related duties not classified under other specific occupations, such as door-to-door sales or demonstration merchandising.

Occupation Name: Door-to-Door Sales Workers, News and Street Vendors, and Related Workers
Description: Sell goods or services door-to-door or on the street.

Occupation Name: Sales and Related Workers, All Other
Description: All sales and related workers not listed separately.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers are responsible for overseeing and managing the daily operations of administrative support staff within an organization. They provide guidance, assign tasks, ensure efficient workflow, and may also be involved in evaluating employee performance and training.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Oversee the work of office and administrative support staff. Assign tasks, train employees, ensure compliance with policies, and manage workflow.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of clerical and administrative support workers.

Communications Equipment Operators typically work in industries such as telecommunications, broadcasting, or emergency services. They operate and monitor various communication equipment, such as switchboards, radio systems, or dispatch consoles. Their responsibilities may include answering and transferring calls, transmitting messages, monitoring communication channels, and providing support during emergencies.
Operate telephone switchboards, route calls, provide information, and record messages. May assist with clerical tasks.
Operate telephone business systems equipment or switchboards to relay incoming, outgoing, and interoffice calls. May supply information to callers and record messages.
Help callers with directory assistance, handle emergency calls, or support specialized telephone systems.

Provide information by accessing alphabetical, geographical, or other directories. Assist customers with special billing requests, such as charges to a third party and credits or refunds for incorrectly dialed numbers or bad connections. May handle emergency calls and assist children or people with physical disabilities to make telephone calls.
Operate or maintain communications devices not included in other categories, possibly handling specialized telecommunication systems.
All communications equipment operators not listed separately.

Financial Clerks perform various clerical and administrative tasks related to financial transactions and records. They work in financial institutions, insurance companies, and other businesses where financial activities are conducted. Some common occupations within this category include billing and posting clerks, payroll clerks, and procurement clerks.
Locate and notify customers of overdue payments, negotiate payment arrangements, and maintain financial records.

Locate and notify customers of delinquent accounts by mail, telephone, or personal visit to solicit payment. Duties include receiving payment and posting amount to customer's account; preparing statements to credit department if customer fails to respond; initiating repossession proceedings or service disconnection; and keeping records of collection and status of accounts.
Compile and record bills for services rendered or goods sold. Verify accuracy and post transactions to customer accounts.
Compile, compute, and record billing, accounting, statistical, and other numerical data for billing purposes. Prepare billing invoices for services rendered or for delivery or shipment of goods.
Prepare and distribute bank statements to customers, answer inquiries, and reconcile discrepancies in records and accounts.

Compile data, compute fees and charges, and prepare invoices for billing purposes. Duties include computing costs and calculating rates for goods, services, and shipment of goods; posting data; and keeping other relevant records. May involve use of computer or typewriter, calculator, and adding and bookkeeping machines.
Compute, classify, and record financial data. Maintain financial records, verify transactions, and reconcile accounts.

Compute, classify, and record numerical data to keep financial records complete. Perform any combination of routine calculating, posting, and verifying duties to obtain primary financial data for use in maintaining accounting records. May also check the accuracy of figures, calculations, and postings pertaining to business transactions recorded by other workers.
Handle cash transactions in casinos, exchange tokens or chips for cash, and balance cash drawers and transactions.

In a gaming establishment, conduct financial transactions for patrons. May reconcile daily summaries of transactions to balance books. May accept patron's credit application and verify credit references to provide check-cashing authorization or to establish house credit accounts. May sell gambling chips, tokens, or tickets to patrons, or to other workers for resale to patrons. May convert gaming chips, tokens, or tickets to currency upon patron's request. May use a cash register or computer to record transaction.
Compile and record employee time data. Calculate wages, deductions, and ensure employees are paid accurately and on time.
Compile and record employee time and payroll data. May compute employees' time worked, production, and commission. May compute and post wages and deductions, or prepare paychecks.
Compile information and records to draw up purchase orders for procurement of materials and services. Track deliveries and maintain vendor data.
Compile information and records to draw up purchase orders for procurement of materials and services.
Receive and pay out money at a financial institution. Track transactions, record deposits, handle withdrawals, and maintain account balances.
Receive and pay out money. Keep records of money and negotiable instruments involved in a financial institution's various transactions.
Perform financial tasks not categorized under other titles, possibly including specialized billing or claims.
All financial clerks not listed separately.

Information and Record Clerks are responsible for maintaining and organizing information, records, and documents in various settings such as libraries, archives, hospitals, and government agencies. They may perform tasks such as data entry, recordkeeping, information retrieval, and assisting users in accessing information.
Assist in securities trading offices by recording and processing stock transactions, verifying trade details, and maintaining client records.

Perform duties related to the purchase, sale or holding of securities. Duties include writing orders for stock purchases or sales, computing transfer taxes, verifying stock transactions, accepting and delivering securities, tracking stock price fluctuations, computing equity, distributing dividends, and keeping records of daily transactions and holdings.
Compose and respond to business correspondence. Review mail requests, direct inquiries, and file outgoing/incoming letters.

Compose letters or electronic correspondence in reply to requests for merchandise, damage claims, credit and other information, delinquent accounts, incorrect billings, or unsatisfactory services. Duties may include gathering data to formulate reply and preparing correspondence.
Perform clerical duties in courts or government offices. Manage records, process licenses, file legal documents, and provide information to the public.

Perform clerical duties for courts of law, municipalities, or governmental licensing agencies and bureaus. May prepare docket of cases to be called; secure information for judges and court; prepare draft agendas or bylaws for town or city council; answer official correspondence; keep fiscal records and accounts; issue licenses or permits; and record data, administer tests, or collect fees.
Perform clerical duties in court of law; prepare docket of cases to be called; secure information for judges; and contact witnesses, attorneys, and litigants to obtain information for court.
Draft agendas and bylaws for town or city council; record minutes of council meetings; answer official correspondence; keep fiscal records and accounts; and prepare reports on civic needs.

Issue licenses or permits to qualified applicants. Obtain necessary information, record data, advise applicants on requirements, collect fees, and issue licenses. May conduct oral, written, visual, or performance testing.
Investigate credit history, verify financial data, and authorize credit limits for customers or businesses.

Authorize credit charges against customers' accounts. Investigate history and credit standing of individuals or business establishments applying for credit. May interview applicants to obtain personal and financial data; determine credit worthiness; process applications; and notify customers of acceptance or rejection of credit.
Authorize credit charges against customers' accounts.

Investigate history and credit standing of individuals or business establishments applying for credit. Telephone or write to credit departments of business and service establishments to obtain information about applicant's credit standing.
Interact with customers, answer questions about products or services, process orders or returns, and handle complaints or billing issues.
Interact with customers to provide information in response to inquiries about products and services and to handle and resolve complaints.
Assist patients in obtaining services, understanding policies and making health care decisions.
Determine eligibility for government aid, benefits, or programs by interviewing applicants, reviewing documentation, and updating records.
Determine eligibility of persons applying to receive assistance from government programs and agency resources, such as welfare, unemployment benefits, social security, and public housing.
Maintain and organize paper and electronic records. Retrieve documents for staff, track file locations, and update records management systems.
File correspondence, cards, invoices, receipts, and other records in alphabetical or numerical order or according to the filing system used. Locate and remove material from file when requested.

Occupation Name: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
Description: Greet and register guests, assign rooms, manage reservations, issue room keys, and process payments. Respond to customer service requests.

Occupation Name: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
Broad Name: Hotel, Motel, and Resort Desk Clerks
Description: Accommodate hotel, motel, and resort patrons by registering and assigning rooms to guests, issuing room keys or cards, transmitting and receiving messages, keeping records of occupied rooms and guests' accounts, making and confirming reservations, and presenting statements to and collecting payments from departing guests.
Ask questions to gather information, often for surveys, market research, or medical histories. Record responses and compile data.

Interview persons by telephone, mail, in person, or by other means for the purpose of completing forms, applications, or questionnaires. Ask specific questions, record answers, and assist persons with completing form. May sort, classify, and file forms.
Help librarians by organizing materials, shelving books, assisting patrons in locating resources, and performing other clerical duties.

Compile records, sort, shelve, issue, and receive library materials such as books, electronic media, pictures, cards, slides and microfilm. Locate library materials for loan and replace material in shelving area, stacks, or files according to identification number and title. Register patrons to permit them to borrow books, periodicals, and other library materials.
Gather financial data from loan applicants, process applications, verify credit information, and prepare loan paperwork for review by loan officers.

Interview loan applicants to elicit information; investigate applicants' backgrounds and verify references; prepare loan request papers; and forward findings, reports, and documents to appraisal department. Review loan papers to ensure completeness, and complete transactions between loan establishment, borrowers, and sellers upon approval of loan.
Interview prospective banking customers, gather personal information, open accounts, and explain account services or policies.
Interview persons desiring to open accounts in financial institutions. Explain account services available to prospective customers and assist them in preparing applications.
Receive and process incoming orders for goods or services. Verify order details, maintain logs, and coordinate shipping or fulfillment.

Receive and process incoming orders for materials, merchandise, classified ads, or services such as repairs, installations, or rental of facilities. Generally receives orders via mail, phone, fax, or other electronic means. Duties include informing customers of receipt, prices, shipping dates, and delays; preparing contracts; and handling complaints.

Occupation Name: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
Description: Support HR departments by maintaining employee records, scheduling interviews, and processing paperwork related to hiring, performance, or termination.

Occupation Name: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
Broad Name: Human Resources Assistants, Except Payroll and Timekeeping
Description: Compile and keep personnel records. Record data for each employee, such as address, weekly earnings, absences, amount of sales or production, supervisory reports, and date of and reason for termination. May prepare reports for employment records, file employment records, or search employee files and furnish information to authorized persons.
Receive and direct visitors, answer telephones, schedule appointments, and provide information about an organization’s services.

Answer inquiries and provide information to the general public, customers, visitors, and other interested parties regarding activities conducted at establishment and location of departments, offices, and employees within the organization.

Occupation Name: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
Description: Make and confirm reservations for transportation or lodging. May issue tickets, provide itinerary information, and assist travelers with changes.

Occupation Name: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
Broad Name: Reservation and Transportation Ticket Agents and Travel Clerks
Description: Make and confirm reservations for transportation or lodging, or sell transportation tickets. May check baggage and direct passengers to designated concourse, pier, or track; deliver tickets, contact individuals and groups to inform them of package tours; or provide tourists with travel or transportation information.
Occupations involving records and information processing not included under other titles. May handle specialized data management, archival tasks, or administrative recordkeeping.

Occupation Name: Information and Record Clerks, All Other
Description: All information and record clerks not listed separately.

Occupation Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers are responsible for tracking, organizing, and coordinating the movement of goods, materials, and resources within various industries. They may perform tasks such as inventory control, order processing, scheduling, and logistics coordination.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Coordinate and track shipments of goods, arrange transportation, handle paperwork, and ensure timely delivery of cargo.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Expedite and route movement of incoming and outgoing cargo and freight shipments in airline, train, and trucking terminals, and shipping docks. Take orders from customers and arrange pickup of freight and cargo for delivery to loading platform. Prepare and examine bills of lading to determine shipping charges and tariffs.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Research rates, routings, or modes of transport for shipment of products. Maintain awareness of regulations affecting the international movement of cargo. Make arrangements for additional services, such as storage or inland transportation.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Transport documents or packages between offices or businesses. Plan routes, obtain signatures, and track deliveries.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Pick up and deliver messages, documents, packages, and other items between offices or departments within an establishment or directly to other business concerns, traveling by foot, bicycle, motorcycle, automobile, or public conveyance.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Schedule and dispatch workers, work crews, or service vehicles for tasks including emergency response, shipping, or repairs. Maintain logs, handle calls, and track operations.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Operate radio, telephone, or computer equipment at emergency response centers. Receive reports from the public of crimes, disturbances, fires, and medical or police emergencies. Relay information to law enforcement and emergency response personnel. May maintain contact with caller until responders arrive.

Occupation Name: Dispatchers, Except Police, Fire, and Ambulance
Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Schedule and dispatch workers, work crews, equipment, or service vehicles for conveyance of materials, freight, or passengers, or for normal installation, service, or emergency repairs rendered outside the place of business. Duties may include using radio, telephone, or computer to transmit assignments and compiling statistics and reports on work progress.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Read utility meters (e.g., gas, water, or electricity), record usage, and check for irregularities or needed maintenance.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Read meter and record consumption of electricity, gas, water, or steam.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Sort, process, and deliver mail. Sell postal products and provide customer service in post offices.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Perform any combination of tasks in a post office, such as receive letters and parcels; sell postage and revenue stamps, postal cards, and stamped envelopes; fill out and sell money orders; place mail in pigeon holes of mail rack or in bags; and examine mail for correct postage.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Sort mail for delivery. Deliver mail on established route by vehicle or on foot.

Occupation Name: Postal Service Mail Sorters, Processors, and Processing Machine Operators
Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution. Examine, sort, and route mail. Load, operate, and occasionally adjust and repair mail processing, sorting, and canceling machinery. Keep records of shipments, pouches, and sacks; and other duties related to mail handling within the postal service.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Coordinate and expedite the flow of work and materials within or between departments according to production schedules.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Coordinate and expedite the flow of work and materials within or between departments of an establishment according to production schedule. Duties include reviewing and distributing production, work, and shipment schedules; conferring with department supervisors to determine progress of work and completion dates; and compiling reports on progress of work, inventory levels, costs, and production problems.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Verify and record incoming or outgoing shipments, prepare items for shipment, and coordinate with carriers. Maintain logs and update shipping records.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Verify and maintain records on incoming and outgoing shipments. Prepare items for shipment. Duties include assembling, addressing, stamping, and shipping merchandise or material; receiving, unpacking, verifying and recording incoming merchandise or material; and arranging for the transportation of products.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Receive, store, and issue merchandise or materials. Track inventory, fill orders, and maintain stockroom organization.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Receive, store, and issue sales floor merchandise, materials, equipment, and other items from stockroom, warehouse, or storage yard to fill shelves, racks, tables, or customers' orders. May mark prices on merchandise and set up sales displays.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Receive, store, and issue sales floor merchandise. Stock shelves, racks, cases, bins, and tables with merchandise and arrange merchandise displays to attract customers. May periodically take physical count of stock or check and mark merchandise.

Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Print and attach price tickets to articles of merchandise using one or several methods, such as marking price on tickets by hand or using ticket-printing machine.

Occupation Name: Stock Clerks- Stockroom, Warehouse, or Storage Yard
Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Receive, store, and issue materials, equipment, and other items from stockroom, warehouse, or storage yard. Keep records and compile stock reports.

Occupation Name: Order Fillers, Wholesale and Retail Sales
Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Fill customers' mail and telephone orders from stored merchandise in accordance with specifications on sales slips or order forms. Duties include computing prices of items, completing order receipts, keeping records of out-going orders, and requisitioning additional materials, supplies, and equipment.

Occupation Name: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Description: Weigh, measure, and check raw materials or products to ensure adherence to standards. Keep relevant records of materials tested or measured.

Occupation Name: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
Minor Name: Material Recording, Scheduling, Dispatching, and Distributing Workers
Broad Name: Weighers, Measurers, Checkers, and Samplers, Recordkeeping
Description: Weigh, measure, and check materials, supplies, and equipment for the purpose of keeping relevant records. Duties are primarily clerical by nature. Includes workers who collect and keep record of samples of products or materials.

Secretaries and Administrative Assistants provide administrative support to organizations and individuals. They perform various tasks, including managing correspondence, scheduling appointments, organizing files, and assisting in office operations.
Perform routine clerical and administrative duties such as scheduling appointments, organizing files, and preparing correspondence.

Occupation Name: Executive Secretaries and Executive Administrative Assistants
Description: Provide high-level administrative support by conducting research, preparing statistical reports, handling information requests, and performing clerical functions such as preparing correspondence, receiving visitors, arranging conference calls, and scheduling meetings. May also train and supervise lower-level clerical staff.

Perform secretarial duties using legal terminology, procedures, and documents. Prepare legal papers and correspondence, such as summonses, complaints, motions, and subpoenas. May also assist with legal research.

Perform secretarial duties using specific knowledge of medical terminology and hospital, clinic, or laboratory procedures. Duties may include scheduling appointments, billing patients, and compiling and recording medical charts, reports, and correspondence.

Occupation Name: Secretaries and Administrative Assistants, Except Legal, Medical, and Executive
Description: Perform routine clerical and administrative functions such as drafting correspondence, scheduling appointments, organizing and maintaining paper and electronic files, or providing information to callers.

Occupation Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: This category includes a wide range of occupations that provide administrative support and perform various clerical tasks within an organization. It encompasses roles such as data entry clerks, mail clerks, office clerks, receptionists, and customer service representatives.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Monitor and control electronic computer systems. Handle hardware or software malfunctions, load peripheral equipment, and oversee system performance.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Monitor and control electronic computer and peripheral electronic data processing equipment to process business, scientific, engineering, and other data according to operating instructions. Monitor and respond to operating and error messages. May enter commands at a computer terminal and set controls on computer and peripheral devices.

Occupation Name: Data Entry and Information Processing Workers
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Input information into computerized databases, spreadsheets, or other systems. Verify accuracy of data and troubleshoot minor input problems.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Data Entry and Information Processing Workers
Description: Operate data entry device, such as keyboard or photo composing perforator. Duties may include verifying data and preparing materials for printing.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Data Entry and Information Processing Workers
Description: Use word processor, computer or typewriter to type letters, reports, forms, or other material from rough draft, corrected copy, or voice recording. May perform other clerical duties as assigned.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Use computer software to format and combine text, data, and graphics into page layouts for print or online publication.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Format typescript and graphic elements using computer software to produce publication-ready material.

Occupation Name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Process insurance applications, changes, or claims. Organize policy details, review claims for completeness, and forward to appropriate departments.

Occupation Name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
Description: Process new insurance policies, modifications to existing policies, and claims forms. Obtain information from policyholders to verify the accuracy and completeness of information on claims forms, applications and related documents, and company records. Update existing policies and company records to reflect changes requested by policyholders and insurance company representatives.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
Description: Obtain information from insured or designated persons for purpose of settling claim with insurance carrier.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Insurance Claims and Policy Processing Clerks
Description: Process applications for, changes to, reinstatement of, and cancellation of insurance policies. Duties include reviewing insurance applications to ensure that all questions have been answered, compiling data on insurance policy changes, changing policy records to conform to insured party's specifications, compiling data on lapsed insurance policies to determine automatic reinstatement according to company policies, canceling insurance policies as requested by agents, and verifying the accuracy of insurance company records.

Occupation Name: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution. Operate mail-processing machines or sort mail by hand.

Occupation Name: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Mail Clerks and Mail Machine Operators, Except Postal Service
Description: Prepare incoming and outgoing mail for distribution. Use hand or mail handling machines to time stamp, open, read, sort, and route incoming mail; and address, seal, stamp, fold, stuff, and affix postage to outgoing mail or packages. Duties may also include keeping necessary records and completed forms.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Perform a variety of administrative tasks, such as answering phones, filing records, and assisting with data entry or scheduling.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Perform duties too varied and diverse to be classified in any specific office clerical occupation, requiring knowledge of office systems and procedures. Clerical duties may be assigned in accordance with the office procedures of individual establishments and may include a combination of answering telephones, bookkeeping, typing or word processing, stenography, office machine operation, and filing.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Operate machines that duplicate, scan, or bind documents. Ensure equipment is maintained and troubleshoot minor mechanical issues.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Operate one or more of a variety of office machines, such as photocopying, photographic, and duplicating machines, or other office machines.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Examine written text for spelling, punctuation, and grammatical errors. Mark corrections and verify revisions.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Read transcript or proof type setup to detect and mark for correction any grammatical, typographical, or compositional errors. Includes proofreaders of Braille.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Compile and compute statistical data under the guidance of statisticians. Prepare tables, charts, or reports summarizing analysis results.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Compile and compute data according to statistical formulas for use in statistical studies. May perform actuarial computations and compile charts and graphs for use by actuaries. Includes actuarial clerks.

Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Apply principles and methods of bioinformatics to assist scientists in areas such as pharmaceuticals, medical technology, biotechnology, computational biology, proteomics, computer information science, biology and medical informatics. Apply bioinformatics tools to visualize, analyze, manipulate or interpret molecular data. May build and maintain databases for processing and analyzing genomic or other biological information.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous Office and Administrative Support Workers
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: Provide a range of administrative services not covered by other standard office occupations, potentially including specialized clerical tasks or recordkeeping.

Occupation Name: Office and Administrative Support Workers, All Other
Minor Name: Other Office and Administrative Support Workers
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Office and Administrative Support Workers
Description: All office and administrative support workers not listed separately.

Concerned with planting, growing, and harvesting crops, raising livestock, catching fish, or managing forest resources. Includes farmers, ranchers, fishers, loggers, and related roles in agricultural or natural environments.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the activities of workers engaged in farming, fishing, and forestry operations. They ensure that tasks are carried out efficiently, adhere to safety regulations, and manage the overall operations of farms, fisheries, or forestry sites.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: Coordinate and direct the activities of agricultural, fishing, or forestry workers. Assign tasks, monitor progress, and ensure compliance with safety and environmental regulations.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of agricultural, forestry, aquacultural, and related workers.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of logging workers.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of aquacultural workers.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Agricultural Crop and Horticultural Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of agricultural crop or horticultural workers.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Animal Husbandry and Animal Care Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Farming, Fishing, and Forestry Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of animal husbandry or animal care workers.

This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the activities of workers engaged in farming, fishing, and forestry operations. They ensure that tasks are carried out efficiently, adhere to safety regulations, and manage the overall operations of farms, fisheries, or forestry sites.
Inspect agricultural commodities or facilities, ensuring compliance with regulations and quality standards. Identify and document violations.
Inspect agricultural commodities, processing equipment, and facilities, and fish and logging operations, to ensure compliance with regulations and laws governing health, quality, and safety.
Select and breed animals according to genetic principles and knowledge of offspring characteristics. Keep records on breeding schedules and pedigrees.

Select and breed animals according to their genealogy, characteristics, and offspring. May require knowledge of artificial insemination techniques and equipment use. May involve keeping records on heats, birth intervals, or pedigree.
Grade, sort, or classify unprocessed food and other agricultural products by size, weight, or condition.
Grade, sort, or classify unprocessed food and other agricultural products by size, weight, color, or condition.
Perform farming or agricultural tasks not covered by other occupations, possibly planting, harvesting, or managing specialized livestock.

Drive and control farm equipment to till soil and to plant, cultivate, and harvest crops. May perform tasks, such as crop baling or hay bucking. May operate stationary equipment to perform post-harvest tasks, such as husking, shelling, threshing, and ginning.

Occupation Name: Farmworkers and Laborers, Crop, Nursery, and Greenhouse
Description: Manually plant, cultivate, and harvest vegetables, fruits, nuts, horticultural specialties, and field crops. Use hand tools, such as shovels, trowels, hoes, tampers, pruning hooks, shears, and knives. Duties may include tilling soil and applying fertilizers; transplanting, weeding, thinning, or pruning crops; applying pesticides; or cleaning, grading, sorting, packing, and loading harvested products. May construct trellises, repair fences and farm buildings, or participate in irrigation activities.
Work in nursery facilities or at customer location planting, cultivating, harvesting, and transplanting trees, shrubs, or plants.

Manually plant, cultivate, and harvest vegetables, fruits, nuts and field crops. Use hand tools, such as shovels, trowels, hoes, tampers, pruning hooks, shears, and knives. Duties may include tilling soil and applying fertilizers; transplanting, weeding, thinning, or pruning crops; applying pesticides; cleaning, packing, and loading harvested products. May construct trellises, repair fences and farm buildings, or participate in irrigation activities.

Occupation Name: Farmworkers, Farm, Ranch, and Aquacultural Animals
Description: Attend to live farm, ranch, or aquacultural animals that may include cattle, sheep, swine, goats, horses and other equines, poultry, finfish, shellfish, and bees. Attend to animals produced for animal products, such as meat, fur, skins, feathers, eggs, milk, and honey. Duties may include feeding, watering, herding, grazing, castrating, branding, de-beaking, weighing, catching, and loading animals. May maintain records on animals; examine animals to detect diseases and injuries; assist in birth deliveries; and administer medications, vaccinations, or insecticides as appropriate. May clean and maintain animal housing areas. Includes workers who shear wool from sheep, and collect eggs in hatcheries.
All agricultural workers not listed separately.

This category includes workers involved in fishing and hunting activities. Fishing workers may engage in various tasks related to commercial or recreational fishing, such as operating fishing vessels, setting nets or lines, and processing or preserving fish. Hunting workers may be involved in activities related to game hunting or wildlife management.
Catch and gather fish or other aquatic species. Maintain fishing gear, navigate vessels, and store catch properly.
Use nets, fishing rods, traps, or other equipment to catch and gather fish or other aquatic animals from rivers, lakes, or oceans, for human consumption or other uses. May haul game onto ship.
Trap and hunt wild animals for food, pelts, or other products. Use knowledge of wildlife habits, tracking techniques, and environmental regulations.
Hunt and trap wild animals for human consumption, fur, feed, bait, or other purposes.

This category includes workers involved in various activities related to forestry, conservation, and logging. It encompasses a range of roles, such as forest workers engaged in planting, maintaining, and harvesting trees; conservation workers involved in preserving and managing natural resources; and logging workers responsible for cutting and processing timber.
Develop, maintain, and protect forests by planting seedlings, controlling insects and diseases, and assisting with fire prevention measures.

Under supervision, perform manual labor necessary to develop, maintain, or protect areas such as forests, forested areas, woodlands, wetlands, and rangelands through such activities as raising and transporting seedlings; combating insects, pests, and diseases harmful to plant life; and building structures to control water, erosion, and leaching of soil. Includes forester aides, seedling pullers, and tree planters.
Fell, process, and transport timber. Operate machinery such as harvesters and loaders, and follow safety protocols when working in forests.
Use axes or chainsaws to fell trees using knowledge of tree characteristics and cutting techniques to control direction of fall and minimize tree damage.

Drive logging tractor or wheeled vehicle equipped with one or more accessories such as bulldozer blade, frontal shear, grapple, logging arch, cable winches, hoisting rack, or crane boom, to fell tree; to skid, load, unload, or stack logs; or to pull stumps or clear brush.
Grade logs or estimate the marketable content or value of logs or pulpwood in sorting yards, millpond, log deck, or similar locations. Inspect logs for defects or measure logs to determine volume.
All logging workers not listed separately.

Involves building, repairing, or demolishing structures and extracting natural resources. Includes carpenters, electricians, miners, plumbers, and other trades focused on infrastructure and resource excavation.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers
Description: This category includes supervisors who oversee construction and extraction activities in various industries. They are responsible for managing and coordinating the work of construction and extraction workers, ensuring compliance with safety regulations, and overseeing the progress of projects. The category encompasses supervisors in fields such as construction, mining, oil and gas extraction, and more.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers
Description: Plan, schedule, and coordinate the work of construction or extraction crews. Monitor progress, enforce safety regulations, and resolve on-site issues.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of construction or extraction workers.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Construction and Extraction Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Construction Trades and Extraction Workers
Description: Direct work crews installing residential or commercial solar photovoltaic or thermal systems.

This category includes various skilled workers involved in construction activities. It encompasses a wide range of occupations such as carpenters, electricians, plumbers, masons, painters, and other tradespeople. These workers perform specialized tasks related to construction, renovation, repair, and maintenance of buildings and structures.
Construct, assemble, and repair boilers, vats, or other large vessels. Use welding or riveting skills to join parts and ensure structural integrity.

Construct, assemble, maintain, and repair stationary steam boilers and boiler house auxiliaries. Align structures or plate sections to assemble boiler frame tanks or vats, following blueprints. Work involves use of hand and power tools, plumb bobs, levels, wedges, dogs, or turnbuckles. Assist in testing assembled vessels. Direct cleaning of boilers and boiler furnaces. Inspect and repair boiler fittings, such as safety valves, regulators, automatic-control mechanisms, water columns, and auxiliary machines.
Build walls, walkways, and other structures using bricks, blocks, or stone. Follow blueprints, mix mortar, and ensure alignment and structural soundness.

Lay and bind building materials, such as brick, structural tile, concrete block, cinder block, glass block, and terra-cotta block, with mortar and other substances to construct or repair walls, partitions, arches, sewers, and other structures.
Build stone structures, such as piers, walls, and abutments. Lay walks, curbstones, or special types of masonry for vats, tanks, and floors.
Construct, install, or repair frameworks and structures. Measure, cut, and shape wood or other materials using hand and power tools.

Construct, erect, install, or repair structures and fixtures made of wood, such as concrete forms; building frameworks, including partitions, joists, studding, and rafters; and wood stairways, window and door frames, and hardwood floors. May also install cabinets, siding, drywall and batt or roll insulation. Includes brattice builders who build doors or brattices (ventilation walls or partitions) in underground passageways.
Construct, erect, install, and repair structures and fixtures of wood, plywood, and wallboard, using carpenter's hand tools and power tools.

Build rough wooden structures, such as concrete forms, scaffolds, tunnel, bridge, or sewer supports, billboard signs, and temporary frame shelters, according to sketches, blueprints, or oral instructions.

Occupation Name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
Description: Install and finish carpets, hardwood, tile, or other flooring materials. Prepare surfaces, align materials, and apply adhesives or finishes.

Broad Name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
Description: Lay and install carpet from rolls or blocks on floors. Install padding and trim flooring materials.

Occupation Name: Floor Layers, Except Carpet, Wood, and Hard Tiles
Broad Name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
Description: Apply blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing, sound-deadening, or decorative coverings to floors.

Broad Name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
Description: Scrape and sand wooden floors to smooth surfaces using floor scraper and floor sanding machine, and apply coats of finish.

Broad Name: Carpet, Floor, and Tile Installers and Finishers
Description: Apply hard tile, marble, and wood tile to walls, floors, ceilings, and roof decks.

Occupation Name: Cement Masons, Concrete Finishers, and Terrazzo Workers
Description: Pour, level, and finish concrete for various projects, such as sidewalks or floors. May also install and finish terrazzo surfaces.

Broad Name: Cement Masons, Concrete Finishers, and Terrazzo Workers
Description: Smooth and finish surfaces of poured concrete, such as floors, walks, sidewalks, roads, or curbs using a variety of hand and power tools. Align forms for sidewalks, curbs, or gutters; patch voids; and use saws to cut expansion joints.

Broad Name: Cement Masons, Concrete Finishers, and Terrazzo Workers
Description: Apply a mixture of cement, sand, pigment, or marble chips to floors, stairways, and cabinet fixtures to fashion durable and decorative surfaces.
Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites, operate hand or power tools, and assist other craft workers.

Perform tasks involving physical labor at construction sites. May operate hand and power tools of all types: air hammers, earth tampers, cement mixers, small mechanical hoists, surveying and measuring equipment, and a variety of other equipment and instruments. May clean and prepare sites, dig trenches, set braces to support the sides of excavations, erect scaffolding, and clean up rubble, debris and other waste materials. May assist other craft workers.
Operate machinery such as bulldozers, excavators, or loaders to move earth and materials, clear land, and assist in building projects.

Occupation Name: Paving, Surfacing, and Tamping Equipment Operators
Description: Operate equipment used for applying concrete, asphalt, or other materials to road beds, parking lots, or airport runways and taxiways, or equipment used for tamping gravel, dirt, or other materials. Includes concrete and asphalt paving machine operators, form tampers, tamping machine operators, and stone spreader operators.

Operate pile drivers mounted on skids, barges, crawler treads, or locomotive cranes to drive pilings for retaining walls, bulkheads, and foundations of structures, such as buildings, bridges, and piers.

Occupation Name: Operating Engineers and Other Construction Equipment Operators
Description: Operate one or several types of power construction equipment, such as motor graders, bulldozers, scrapers, compressors, pumps, derricks, shovels, tractors, or front-end loaders to excavate, move, and grade earth, erect structures, or pour concrete or other hard surface pavement. May repair and maintain equipment in addition to other duties.

Occupation Name: Drywall Installers, Ceiling Tile Installers, and Tapers
Description: Install wallboard and apply tape or compound to seams and corners for finishing. May also install ceiling tiles in buildings.

Broad Name: Drywall Installers, Ceiling Tile Installers, and Tapers
Description: Apply plasterboard or other wallboard to ceilings or interior walls of buildings. Apply or mount acoustical tiles or blocks, strips, or sheets of shock-absorbing materials to ceilings and walls of buildings to reduce or reflect sound. Materials may be of decorative quality. Includes lathers who fasten wooden, metal, or rockboard lath to walls, ceilings or partitions of buildings to provide support base for plaster, fire-proofing, or acoustical material.

Broad Name: Drywall Installers, Ceiling Tile Installers, and Tapers
Description: Seal joints between plasterboard or other wallboard to prepare wall surface for painting or papering.
Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, lighting, and control systems. Diagnose issues, ensure compliance with codes, and follow safety protocols.

Install, maintain, and repair electrical wiring, equipment, and fixtures. Ensure that work is in accordance with relevant codes. May install or service street lights, intercom systems, or electrical control systems.
Install glass in windows, skylights, and other fixtures in buildings or vehicles. Measure and cut glass, seal edges, and secure frames.
Install glass in windows, skylights, store fronts, and display cases, or on surfaces, such as building fronts, interior walls, ceilings, and tabletops.
Line and cover structures with insulating materials to control or maintain temperatures. May apply insulating materials to pipes, ductwork, or other mechanical systems.

Occupation Name: Insulation Workers, Floor, Ceiling, and Wall
Description: Line and cover structures with insulating materials. May work with batt, roll, or blown insulation materials.
Apply insulating materials to pipes or ductwork, or other mechanical systems in order to help control and maintain temperature.
Apply paint, stain, varnish, or wallpaper to buildings, equipment, or other structures. Prepare surfaces by cleaning or sanding, and mix materials to achieve desired finishes.

Paint walls, equipment, buildings, bridges, and other structural surfaces, using brushes, rollers, and spray guns. May remove old paint to prepare surface prior to painting. May mix colors or oils to obtain desired color or consistency.

Cover interior walls or ceilings of rooms with decorative wallpaper or fabric, or attach advertising posters on surfaces such as walls and billboards. May remove old materials or prepare surfaces to be papered.
Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, water mains, or gas lines. Install and repair plumbing fixtures, pipe systems, or steam systems.
Lay pipe for storm or sanitation sewers, drains, and water mains. Perform any combination of the following tasks: grade trenches or culverts, position pipe, or seal joints.

Assemble, install, alter, and repair pipelines or pipe systems that carry water, steam, air, or other liquids or gases. May install heating and cooling equipment and mechanical control systems. Includes sprinklerfitters.

Lay out, assemble, install, or maintain pipe systems, pipe supports, or related hydraulic or pneumatic equipment for steam, hot water, heating, cooling, lubricating, sprinkling, or industrial production or processing systems.
Assemble, install, or repair pipes, fittings, or fixtures of heating, water, or drainage systems, according to specifications or plumbing codes.
Apply plaster or stucco to walls and ceilings, forming smooth or textured surfaces. May also install prefabricated exterior insulation systems.
Apply interior or exterior plaster, cement, stucco, or similar materials. May also set ornamental plaster.
Position and secure steel bars or mesh in concrete forms to reinforce concrete structures. Cut, bend, or weld rebar as necessary.
Position and secure steel bars or mesh in concrete forms in order to reinforce concrete. Use a variety of fasteners, rod-bending machines, blowtorches, and hand tools. Includes rod busters.
Cover roofs of structures with shingles, asphalt, or other materials. Install insulation layers, apply waterproofing, and ensure correct sealing to prevent leaks.

Cover roofs of structures with shingles, slate, asphalt, aluminum, wood, or related materials. May spray roofs, sidings, and walls with material to bind, seal, insulate, or soundproof sections of structures.
Fabricate, assemble, and install products made from thin metal sheets, such as ducts or roofing panels. Use technical drawings, cut metal, and secure seams.

Fabricate, assemble, install, and repair sheet metal products and equipment, such as ducts, control boxes, drainpipes, and furnace casings. Work may involve any of the following: setting up and operating fabricating machines to cut, bend, and straighten sheet metal; shaping metal over anvils, blocks, or forms using hammer; operating soldering and welding equipment to join sheet metal parts; or inspecting, assembling, and smoothing seams and joints of burred surfaces. Includes sheet metal duct installers who install prefabricated sheet metal ducts used for heating, air conditioning, or other purposes.
Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form frameworks for buildings, bridges, and other structures.

Raise, place, and unite iron or steel girders, columns, and other structural members to form completed structures or structural frameworks. May erect metal storage tanks and assemble prefabricated metal buildings.
Assemble, install, and maintain solar photovoltaic systems on roofs or other structures. Ensure safe handling of electrical wiring and compliance with building codes.

Assemble, install, or maintain solar photovoltaic (PV) systems on roofs or other structures in compliance with site assessment and schematics. May include measuring, cutting, assembling, and bolting structural framing and solar modules. May perform minor electrical work such as current checks.

This category includes workers who assist skilled tradespeople in various construction trades. They provide support and assistance in tasks such as carrying materials, cleaning work areas, operating machinery, and performing other duties as directed by the skilled trades workers. Helpers work under the supervision of more experienced tradespeople and contribute to the overall progress of construction projects.
Assist skilled construction trades workers by supplying or holding materials or tools, cleaning job sites, and performing basic tasks under the direction of more experienced craft workers.

Occupation Name: Helpers--Brickmasons, Blockmasons, Stonemasons, and Tile and Marble Setters
Description: Help brickmasons, blockmasons, stonemasons, or tile and marble setters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.
Help carpenters by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.
Help electricians by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.

Occupation Name: Helpers--Painters, Paperhangers, Plasterers, and Stucco Masons
Description: Help painters, paperhangers, plasterers, or stucco masons by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.
Help plumbers, pipefitters, steamfitters, or pipelayers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.
Help roofers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include using, supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.
All construction trades helpers not listed separately.

This category includes a diverse range of construction and related workers who perform various tasks that support construction projects but do not fall into other specific construction trades categories. It may include workers such as highway maintenance workers, roustabouts, elevator installers and repairers, and other construction-related roles that are not classified elsewhere.
Inspect buildings, highways, and other structures to ensure compliance with building codes and regulations. Review structural quality, safety, and overall integrity of construction projects.

Inspect structures using engineering skills to determine structural soundness and compliance with specifications, building codes, and other regulations. Inspections may be general in nature or may be limited to a specific area, such as electrical systems or plumbing.
Assemble, install, and repair elevators, escalators, and similar systems. Read blueprints, conduct routine maintenance, and troubleshoot mechanical or electrical malfunctions.
Assemble, install, repair, or maintain electric or hydraulic freight or passenger elevators, escalators, or dumbwaiters.
Build and repair fences, gates, and related enclosures. Measure property lines, dig postholes, and set fence posts in concrete or other materials.
Erect and repair fences and fence gates, using hand and power tools.
Identify, remove, package, transport, or dispose of hazardous substances (like asbestos or lead). Follow strict safety protocols to protect health and the environment.

Identify, remove, pack, transport, or dispose of hazardous materials, including asbestos, lead-based paint, waste oil, fuel, transmission fluid, radioactive materials, or contaminated soil. Specialized training and certification in hazardous materials handling or a confined entry permit are generally required. May operate earth-moving equipment or trucks.
Maintain highways, roads, and airport runways. Patch potholes, clear drains, remove snow, and set up traffic control devices.

Maintain highways, municipal and rural roads, airport runways, and rights-of-way. Duties include patching broken or eroded pavement, repairing guard rails, highway markers, and snow fences. May also mow or clear brush from along road or plow snow from roadway.

Occupation Name: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
Description: Operate machinery to lay, repair, or remove railroad tracks. Measure and cut rails, align track sections, and ensure proper alignment and safety.

Occupation Name: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
Broad Name: Rail-Track Laying and Maintenance Equipment Operators
Description: Lay, repair, and maintain track for standard or narrow-gauge railroad equipment used in regular railroad service or in plant yards, quarries, sand and gravel pits, and mines. Includes ballast cleaning machine operators and railroad bed tamping machine operators.

Occupation Name: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
Description: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or drains. Locate problem areas, operate pumping equipment, and perform routine system maintenance.

Occupation Name: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
Broad Name: Septic Tank Servicers and Sewer Pipe Cleaners
Description: Clean and repair septic tanks, sewer lines, or drains. May patch walls and partitions of tank, replace damaged drain tile, or repair breaks in underground piping.
Carry out construction-related tasks not categorized under specific trades. May include highway flagging, site preparation, or specialized tasks such as chimney repair.
Lay out, cut, and place segmental paving units. Includes installers of bedding and restraining materials for the paving units.

Occupation Name: Construction and Related Workers, All Other
Description: All construction and related workers not listed separately.
Install or repair solar energy systems designed to collect, store, and circulate solar-heated water for residential, commercial or industrial use.

Perform a variety of activities to weatherize homes and make them more energy efficient. Duties include repairing windows, insulating ducts, and performing heating, ventilating, and air-conditioning (HVAC) work. May perform energy audits and advise clients on energy conservation measures.

This category includes workers involved in extracting natural resources from the earth. It encompasses various occupations such as mining machine operators, oil and gas extraction workers, quarrying workers, and other related roles. These workers are primarily engaged in extracting minerals, metals, oil, gas, and other valuable resources from the ground.

Occupation Name: Derrick, Rotary Drill, and Service Unit Operators, Oil, Gas, and Mining
Description: Operate derricks and drilling equipment to extract oil, gas, or minerals from the earth. Monitor pressure gauges, maintain equipment, and manage the drilling process.

Broad Name: Derrick, Rotary Drill, and Service Unit Operators, Oil, Gas, and Mining
Description: Rig derrick equipment and operate pumps to circulate mud through drill hole.

Occupation Name: Rotary Drill Operators, Oil and Gas
Broad Name: Derrick, Rotary Drill, and Service Unit Operators, Oil, Gas, and Mining
Description: Set up or operate a variety of drills to remove underground oil and gas, or remove core samples for testing during oil and gas exploration.

Occupation Name: Service Unit Operators, Oil, Gas, and Mining
Broad Name: Derrick, Rotary Drill, and Service Unit Operators, Oil, Gas, and Mining
Description: Operate equipment to increase oil flow from producing wells or to remove stuck pipe, casing, tools, or other obstructions from drilling wells. May also perform similar services in mining exploration operations. Includes fishing-tool technicians.

Occupation Name: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
Description: Operate drilling equipment to drill holes for utility lines, foundation supports, or geological exploration. Monitor equipment performance, remove earth or rock, and ensure site safety.

Occupation Name: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
Broad Name: Earth Drillers, Except Oil and Gas
Description: Operate a variety of drills such as rotary, churn, and pneumatic to tap sub-surface water and salt deposits, to remove core samples during mineral exploration or soil testing, and to facilitate the use of explosives in mining or construction. May use explosives. Includes horizontal and earth boring machine operators.

Occupation Name: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
Description: Handle explosives for construction, mining, or demolition. Assess rock or other material, set charges, and detonate explosives following strict safety protocols.

Occupation Name: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
Broad Name: Explosives Workers, Ordnance Handling Experts, and Blasters
Description: Place and detonate explosives to demolish structures or to loosen, remove, or displace earth, rock, or other materials. May perform specialized handling, storage, and accounting procedures. Includes seismograph shooters.
Operate self-propelled machines to extract coal, ore, or other materials from mines. Monitor equipment gauges, manage conveyor systems, and ensure efficient extraction.
Operate self-propelled mining machines that rip coal, metal and nonmetal ores, rock, stone, or sand from the mine face and load it onto conveyors or into shuttle cars in a continuous operation.

Occupation Name: Mine Cutting and Channeling Machine Operators
Description: Operate machinery such as longwall shears, plows, and cutting machines to cut or channel along the face or seams of coal mines, stone quarries, or other mining surfaces to facilitate blasting, separating, or removing minerals or materials from mines or from the Earth's surface. Includes shale planers.
All mining machine operators not listed separately.
Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using drills, wedges, or other tools. Check for quality, measure, and mark cutting lines.
Separate blocks of rough dimension stone from quarry mass using jackhammer and wedges.
Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mines to prevent roof collapses. Monitor and test the stability of installed bolts.
Operate machinery to install roof support bolts in underground mine.
Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform basic maintenance, transport materials, and maintain safety standards on oil rigs or fields.
Assemble or repair oil field equipment using hand and power tools. Perform other tasks as needed.
Assist more experienced workers in oil, gas, or mining operations. Haul materials, operate simple equipment, and clean worksites under close supervision.

Help extraction craft workers, such as earth drillers, blasters and explosives workers, derrick operators, and mining machine operators, by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying equipment or cleaning work area.
Perform extraction tasks not elsewhere classified, such as specialized drilling or rare mineral sampling in mines or quarries.
All extraction workers not listed separately.

Covers roles setting up, troubleshooting, and fixing equipment, machines, and systems. Occupations include automotive mechanics, HVAC installers, and general maintenance technicians working across various industries.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
Description: This category includes supervisors who oversee and coordinate the work of installation, maintenance, and repair workers across various industries. They are responsible for managing teams, assigning tasks, ensuring compliance with safety regulations, and maintaining the efficiency of installation and repair processes. Supervisors in this category may work in fields such as construction, manufacturing, telecommunications, utilities, and transportation.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
Description: Direct and coordinate maintenance or repair staff. Assign tasks, schedule work, ensure compliance with safety regulations, and track work progress.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Minor Name: Supervisors of Installation, Maintenance, and Repair Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of mechanics, installers, and repairers.

Occupation Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Description: This category includes workers who install, maintain, and repair electrical and electronic equipment across various industries. They may work on equipment such as electrical systems, telecommunications equipment, computer systems, and audiovisual systems. Workers in this category are skilled in diagnosing and fixing electrical and electronic issues, reading technical diagrams and manuals, and using specialized tools and equipment.

Occupation Name: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
Minor Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Description: Install, maintain, and repair business machines such as computers, ATMs, copiers, or printers. Diagnose hardware problems, replace parts, and test functionality.

Occupation Name: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
Minor Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Broad Name: Computer, Automated Teller, and Office Machine Repairers
Description: Repair, maintain, or install computers, word processing systems, automated teller machines, and electronic office machines, such as duplicating and fax machines.

Occupation Name: Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers
Minor Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Description: Install and maintain radio or telecommunications equipment (cell towers, broadcast transmitters, etc.). Diagnose signal issues, update equipment, and perform routine inspections.

Occupation Name: Radio, Cellular, and Tower Equipment Installers and Repairs
Minor Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Broad Name: Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers
Description: Repair, install or maintain mobile or stationary radio transmitting, broadcasting, and receiving equipment, and two-way radio communications systems used in cellular telecommunications, mobile broadband, ship-to-shore, aircraft-to-ground communications, and radio equipment in service and emergency vehicles. May test and analyze network coverage.

Minor Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Broad Name: Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers
Description: Test or repair mobile or stationary radio transmitting and receiving equipment and two-way radio communications systems used in ship-to-shore communications and found in service and emergency vehicles.

Occupation Name: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
Minor Name: Electrical and Electronic Equipment Mechanics, Installers, and Repairers
Broad Name: Radio and Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers
