Produce and repair dies, jigs, fixtures, or specialized tools used in manufacturing. Use precision instruments and follow engineering specifications.
Analyze specifications, lay out metal stock, set up and operate machine tools, and fit and assemble parts to make and repair dies, cutting tools, jigs, fixtures, gauges, and machinists' hand tools.
Join metal parts together or repair them using welding, soldering, or brazing equipment. Inspect welds, maintain equipment, and follow safety measures.
Use hand-welding, flame-cutting, hand soldering, or brazing equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products.
Use hand-welding or flame-cutting equipment to weld or join metal components or to fill holes, indentations, or seams of fabricated metal products.
Braze or solder together components to assemble fabricated metal parts, using soldering iron, torch, or welding machine and flux.

Occupation Name: Welding, Soldering, and Brazing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend welding, soldering, or brazing machines or robots that weld, braze, solder, or heat treat metal products, components, or assemblies. Includes workers who operate laser cutters or laser-beam machines.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
Description: Carry out metal- or plastic-working processes not specifically classified under other job titles. May include finishing, polishing, or specialized shaping tasks.

Occupation Name: Heat Treating Equipment Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
Description: Set up, operate, or tend heating equipment, such as heat-treating furnaces, flame-hardening machines, induction machines, soaking pits, or vacuum equipment to temper, harden, anneal, or heat-treat metal or plastic objects.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
Description: Lay out reference points and dimensions on metal or plastic stock or workpieces, such as sheets, plates, tubes, structural shapes, castings, or machine parts, for further processing. Includes shipfitters.

Occupation Name: Plating and Coating Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
Description: Set up, operate, or tend plating or coating machines to coat metal or plastic products with chromium, zinc, copper, cadmium, nickel, or other metal to protect or decorate surfaces. Includes electrolytic processes.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
Description: Perform precision smoothing, sharpening, polishing, or grinding of metal objects.

Occupation Name: Metal Workers and Plastic Workers, All Other
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Metal Workers and Plastic Workers
Description: All metal workers and plastic workers not listed separately.

Printing Workers are involved in various tasks related to the printing industry, including operating printing presses, preparing materials for printing, performing quality checks, and maintaining printing equipment. This category encompasses roles such as prepress technicians, press operators, bindery workers, and finishing workers. Printing workers may be employed in commercial printing companies, publishing houses, packaging companies, or specialized printing shops.
Operate and maintain printing presses or digital printing equipment, set up print jobs, and handle tasks like color management, binding, and finishing.
Format and proof text and images submitted by designers and clients into finished pages that can be printed. Includes digital and photo typesetting. May produce printing plates.
Set up and operate digital, letterpress, lithographic, flexographic, gravure, or other printing machines. Includes short-run offset printing presses.
Bind books and other publications or finish printed products by hand or machine. May set up binding and finishing machines.

Occupations within the category "51-6000 Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers" typically involve various processes related to the production of clothing, textiles, and furnishings. This includes but is not limited to sewing, upholstering, tailoring, and weaving.
Operate washing or dry-cleaning machines to clean garments or other articles. Sort items, treat stains, and press or fold finished laundry.

Operate or tend washing or dry-cleaning machines to wash or dry-clean industrial or household articles, such as cloth garments, suede, leather, furs, blankets, draperies, linens, rugs, and carpets. Includes spotters and dyers of these articles.

Occupation Name: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
Description: Press or shape garments using hand irons or pressing machines. Smooth or finish fabrics for sale or further processing.

Occupation Name: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
Broad Name: Pressers, Textile, Garment, and Related Materials
Description: Press or shape articles by hand or machine.
Operate sewing machines to stitch, join, or hem fabrics, garments, or non-garment items. Follow patterns and check finished seams.
Operate or tend sewing machines to join, reinforce, decorate, or perform related sewing operations in the manufacture of garment or nongarment products.
Construct, decorate, or repair leather products such as shoes, handbags, or saddles. Cut, stitch, and finish materials following patterns or designs.

Occupation Name: Shoe and Leather Workers and Repairers
Description: Construct, decorate, or repair leather and leather-like products, such as luggage, shoes, and saddles.
Operate or tend a variety of machines to join, decorate, reinforce, or finish shoes and shoe parts.
Customize or sew garments, measure clients, alter clothing, and design or repair various apparel items.
Sew, join, reinforce, or finish, usually with needle and thread, a variety of manufactured items. Includes weavers and stitchers.
Design, make, alter, repair, or fit garments.

Occupation Name: Textile Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Operate machines that weave, knit, or otherwise process textiles. Monitor operations, handle thread or fabric changes, and clear machine jams.

Occupation Name: Textile Bleaching and Dyeing Machine Operators and Tenders
Broad Name: Textile Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend machines to bleach, shrink, wash, dye, or finish textiles or synthetic or glass fibers.

Occupation Name: Textile Cutting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Textile Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut textiles.

Occupation Name: Textile Knitting and Weaving Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Textile Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that knit, loop, weave, or draw in textiles.

Occupation Name: Textile Winding, Twisting, and Drawing Out Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Textile Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that wind or twist textiles; or draw out and combine sliver, such as wool, hemp, or synthetic fibers. Includes slubber machine and drawing frame operators.

Occupation Name: Miscellaneous Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
Description: Perform textile- or furnishings-related tasks not classified elsewhere, possibly involving specialized finishing, drapery work, or craft-based textile production.

Occupation Name: Extruding and Forming Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Synthetic and Glass Fibers
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that extrude and form continuous filaments from synthetic materials, such as liquid polymer, rayon, and fiberglass.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
Description: Draw and construct sets of precision master fabric patterns or layouts. May also mark and cut fabrics and apparel.

Broad Name: Miscellaneous Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
Description: Make, repair, or replace upholstery for household furniture or transportation vehicles.

Occupation Name: Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers, All Other
Broad Name: Miscellaneous Textile, Apparel, and Furnishings Workers
Description: All textile, apparel, and furnishings workers not listed separately.

The "51-7000 Woodworkers" occupational category typically includes jobs that involve working with wood to create various types of products. This can range from furniture to musical instruments and more.
Build and repair wooden cabinets, furniture, or fixtures. Read blueprints, measure and cut wood, assemble components, and finish surfaces.

Cut, shape, and assemble wooden articles or set up and operate a variety of woodworking machines, such as power saws, jointers, and mortisers to surface, cut, or shape lumber or to fabricate parts for wood products.
Shape, finish, or refinish new or repaired furniture. Remove old finishes, apply stains or sealers, and polish surfaces for desired appearance.
Shape, finish, and refinish damaged, worn, or used furniture or new high-grade furniture to specified color or finish.
Plan, lay out, and construct wooden precision models or patterns for use in manufacturing. Operate tools and machinery to shape wood according to specs.
Construct full-size and scale wooden precision models of products. Includes wood jig builders and loft workers.
Plan, lay out, and construct wooden unit or sectional patterns used in forming sand molds for castings.

Occupation Name: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up and operate machines such as saws, molders, or sanders to cut and shape wood. Monitor operation, adjust settings, and ensure correct dimensions.

Occupation Name: Sawing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Wood
Broad Name: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend wood sawing machines. May operate CNC equipment. Includes lead sawyers.

Occupation Name: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Except Sawing
Broad Name: Woodworking Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend woodworking machines, such as drill presses, lathes, shapers, routers, sanders, planers, and wood nailing machines. May operate CNC equipment.
Perform specialized or various woodworking duties not specified under other job titles, potentially including custom carving, lathe work, or wood pattern finishing.
All woodworkers not listed separately.

The "51-8000 Plant and System Operators" occupational category typically involves jobs that control and operate industrial plants or systems, such as power plants, water treatment facilities, or chemical processing plants.

Occupation Name: Power Plant Operators, Distributors, and Dispatchers
Description: Control or operate machinery that generates electric power. Monitor instruments, regulate power flows, and manage distribution to meet demand.

Broad Name: Power Plant Operators, Distributors, and Dispatchers
Description: Operate or control nuclear reactors. Move control rods, start and stop equipment, monitor and adjust controls, and record data in logs. Implement emergency procedures when needed. May respond to abnormalities, determine cause, and recommend corrective action.

Broad Name: Power Plant Operators, Distributors, and Dispatchers
Description: Coordinate, regulate, or distribute electricity or steam.

Broad Name: Power Plant Operators, Distributors, and Dispatchers
Description: Control, operate, or maintain machinery to generate electric power. Includes auxiliary equipment operators.
Operate and maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment. Adjust controls, perform inspections, and ensure safe pressure and temperature levels.

Operate or maintain stationary engines, boilers, or other mechanical equipment to provide utilities for buildings or industrial processes. Operate equipment, such as steam engines, generators, motors, turbines, and steam boilers.

Occupation Name: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
Description: Run or control treatment processes to purify water or treat sewage. Monitor operating conditions, record test results, and adjust equipment to meet standards.

Occupation Name: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
Broad Name: Water and Wastewater Treatment Plant and System Operators
Description: Operate or control an entire process or system of machines, often through the use of control boards, to transfer or treat water or wastewater.
Oversee or operate specialized plant systems not under other classifications—e.g., nuclear reactor operators or specific chemical processing systems.
Control or operate entire chemical processes or system of machines.
Distribute or process gas for utility companies and others by controlling compressors to maintain specified pressures on main pipelines.

Occupation Name: Petroleum Pump System Operators, Refinery Operators, and Gaugers
Description: Operate or control petroleum refining or processing units. May specialize in controlling manifold and pumping systems, gauging or testing oil in storage tanks, or regulating the flow of oil into pipelines.

Occupation Name: Plant and System Operators, All Other
Description: All plant and system operators not listed separately.

Calculate, measure, load, mix, and process refined feedstock with additives in fermentation or reaction process vessels and monitor production process. Perform, and keep records of, plant maintenance, repairs, and safety inspections.
Monitor, operate, and maintain landfill gas collection system components and environmental monitoring and control systems.
Control and monitor biomass plant activities and perform maintenance as needed.

Monitor and control activities associated with hydropower generation. Operate plant equipment, such as turbines, pumps, valves, gates, fans, electric control boards, and battery banks. Monitor equipment operation and performance and make necessary adjustments to ensure optimal performance. Perform equipment maintenance and repair as necessary.

The category "51-9000 Other Production Occupations" involves a wide array of jobs that generally revolve around producing, processing, or preparing consumer goods in various industries, such as food processing, manufacturing, and more.

Occupation Name: Chemical Processing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend equipment that processes chemicals. Observe gauges, take samples, and regulate flow, temperature, or pressure.

Broad Name: Chemical Processing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend equipment to control chemical changes or reactions in the processing of industrial or consumer products. Equipment used includes devulcanizers, steam-jacketed kettles, and reactor vessels.

Occupation Name: Separating, Filtering, Clarifying, Precipitating, and Still Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Chemical Processing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend continuous flow or vat-type equipment; filter presses; shaker screens; centrifuges; condenser tubes; precipitating, fermenting, or evaporating tanks; scrubbing towers; or batch stills. These machines extract, sort, or separate liquids, gases, or solids from other materials to recover a refined product. Includes dairy processing equipment operators.

Occupation Name: Crushing, Grinding, Polishing, Mixing, and Blending Workers
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that crush, grind, or blend materials (e.g., coal, glass, spices). Verify consistency and quality of output.

Occupation Name: Crushing, Grinding, and Polishing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Crushing, Grinding, Polishing, Mixing, and Blending Workers
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to crush, grind, or polish materials, such as coal, glass, grain, stone, food, or rubber.

Broad Name: Crushing, Grinding, Polishing, Mixing, and Blending Workers
Description: Grind, sand, or polish, using hand tools or hand-held power tools, a variety of metal, wood, stone, clay, plastic, or glass objects. Includes chippers, buffers, and finishers.

Occupation Name: Mixing and Blending Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Crushing, Grinding, Polishing, Mixing, and Blending Workers
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to mix or blend materials, such as chemicals, tobacco, liquids, color pigments, or explosive ingredients.
Use hand or machine cutters to trim, cut, or slice materials (fabric, paper, metal) for further processing. Follow patterns or templates.
Use hand tools or hand-held power tools to cut and trim a variety of manufactured items, such as carpet, fabric, stone, glass, or rubber.

Occupation Name: Cutting and Slicing Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines that cut or slice materials, such as glass, stone, cork, rubber, tobacco, food, paper, or insulating material.

Occupation Name: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Operate equipment that extrudes or forms materials such as clay, glass, or rubber into shapes. Adjust settings, remove finished products, and inspect for defects.

Occupation Name: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Broad Name: Extruding, Forming, Pressing, and Compacting Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines, such as glass forming machines, plodder machines, and tuber machines, to shape and form products, such as glassware, food, rubber, soap, brick, tile, clay, wax, tobacco, or cosmetics.

Occupation Name: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
Description: Operate heating equipment used in manufacturing. Control temperature, feed raw materials, and monitor the process to ensure proper treatment or drying.

Occupation Name: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
Broad Name: Furnace, Kiln, Oven, Drier, and Kettle Operators and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend heating equipment other than basic metal, plastic, or food processing equipment. Includes activities, such as annealing glass, drying lumber, curing rubber, removing moisture from materials, or boiling soap.

Occupation Name: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
Description: Examine products or materials for defects, measure weights, and ensure items meet specifications. Record findings and recommend adjustments.

Occupation Name: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
Broad Name: Inspectors, Testers, Sorters, Samplers, and Weighers
Description: Inspect, test, sort, sample, or weigh nonagricultural raw materials or processed, machined, fabricated, or assembled parts or products for defects, wear, and deviations from specifications. May use precision measuring instruments and complex test equipment.

Occupation Name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
Description: Design, fabricate, adjust, or repair jewelry and precious metal pieces. Cut and set gemstones, solder metal parts, and polish final products.

Occupation Name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
Broad Name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
Description: Design, fabricate, adjust, repair, or appraise jewelry, gold, silver, other precious metals, or gems. Includes diamond polishers and gem cutters, and persons who perform precision casting and modeling of molds, casting metal in molds, or setting precious and semi-precious stones for jewelry and related products.

Broad Name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
Description: Fabricate and repair jewelry articles. Make models or molds to create jewelry items.

Broad Name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
Description: Fabricate, finish, or evaluate the quality of gems and diamonds used in jewelry or industrial tools.

Broad Name: Jewelers and Precious Stone and Metal Workers
Description: Cast, anneal, solder, hammer, or shape gold, silver, pewter or other metals to form jewelry or other metal items such as goblets or candlesticks.

Occupation Name: Medical, Dental, and Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
Description: Construct, fit, or repair medical devices such as dentures, eyeglasses, or prosthetics. Use specialized machinery, molds, or measuring equipment.

Broad Name: Medical, Dental, and Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
Description: Construct and repair full or partial dentures or dental appliances.

Broad Name: Medical, Dental, and Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
Description: Construct, fit, maintain, or repair medical supportive devices, such as braces, orthotics and prosthetic devices, joints, arch supports, and other surgical and medical appliances.

Broad Name: Medical, Dental, and Ophthalmic Laboratory Technicians
Description: Cut, grind, and polish eyeglasses, contact lenses, or other precision optical elements. Assemble and mount lenses into frames or process other optical elements. Includes precision lens polishers or grinders, centerer-edgers, and lens mounters.

Occupation Name: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
Description: Run machines that prepare and package products for shipping. Fill containers, seal packages, label items, and ensure quality control.

Occupation Name: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
Broad Name: Packaging and Filling Machine Operators and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend machines to prepare industrial or consumer products for storage or shipment. Includes cannery workers who pack food products.
Paint or coat a variety of products, including vehicles, furniture, or machinery. May use spray guns, rollers, or brushes.

Occupation Name: Coating, Painting, and Spraying Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend machines to coat or paint any of a wide variety of products, including glassware, cloth, ceramics, metal, plastic, paper, or wood, with lacquer, silver, copper, rubber, varnish, glaze, enamel, oil, or rust-proofing materials.
Operate or tend painting machines to paint surfaces of transportation equipment, such as automobiles, buses, trucks, trains, boats, and airplanes. Includes painters in auto body repair facilities.
Paint, coat, or decorate articles such as furniture, glass, plateware, pottery, jewelry, toys, books, or leather.
Perform tasks in the manufacturing of electronic semiconductors. Monitor equipment, measure chemical solutions, and inspect wafers for defects.

Perform any or all of the following functions in the manufacture of electronic semiconductors: load semiconductor material into furnace; saw formed ingots into segments; load individual segment into crystal growing chamber and monitor controls; locate crystal axis in ingot using x-ray equipment and saw ingots into wafers; and clean, polish, and load wafers into series of special purpose furnaces, chemical baths, and equipment used to form circuitry and change conductive properties.

Occupation Name: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
Description: Develop film or operate digital printing equipment. Adjust chemical mixes, maintain darkroom or digital lab equipment, and oversee final print quality.

Occupation Name: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
Broad Name: Photographic Process Workers and Processing Machine Operators
Description: Perform work involved in developing and processing photographic images from film or digital media. May perform precision tasks such as editing photographic negatives and prints.
Engage in diverse production roles not classified under a specific category, such as tire builders, fabricated metal workers, or factory line positions handling specialized tasks.

Occupation Name: Adhesive Bonding Machine Operators and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend bonding machines that use adhesives to join items for further processing or to form a completed product. Processes include joining veneer sheets into plywood; gluing paper; or joining rubber and rubberized fabric parts, plastic, simulated leather, or other materials.

Occupation Name: Cleaning, Washing, and Metal Pickling Equipment Operators and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend machines to wash or clean products, such as barrels or kegs, glass items, tin plate, food, pulp, coal, plastic, or rubber, to remove impurities.

Occupation Name: Cooling and Freezing Equipment Operators and Tenders
Description: Operate or tend equipment, such as cooling and freezing units, refrigerators, batch freezers, and freezing tunnels, to cool or freeze products, food, blood plasma, and chemicals.
Engrave or etch metal, wood, rubber, or other materials. Includes such workers as etcher-circuit processors, pantograph engravers, and silk screen etchers.

Occupation Name: Molders, Shapers, and Casters, Except Metal and Plastic
Description: Mold, shape, form, cast, or carve products such as food products, figurines, tile, pipes, and candles consisting of clay, glass, plaster, concrete, stone, or combinations of materials.
Cut or carve stone according to diagrams and patterns.

Occupation Name: Glass Blowers, Molders, Benders, and Finishers
Description: Shape molten glass according to patterns.
Operate production machines such as pug mill, jigger machine, or potter's wheel to process clay in manufacture of ceramic, pottery and stoneware products.
Perform a variety of duties such as mixing materials, assembling mold parts, filling molds, and stacking molds to mold and cast a wide range of products.

Occupation Name: Paper Goods Machine Setters, Operators, and Tenders
Description: Set up, operate, or tend paper goods machines that perform a variety of functions, such as converting, sawing, corrugating, banding, wrapping, boxing, stitching, forming, or sealing paper or paperboard sheets into products.
Operate machines to build tires.
Help production workers by performing duties requiring less skill. Duties include supplying or holding materials or tools, and cleaning work area and equipment.
All production workers not listed separately.
Prepare and sort materials or products for recycling. Identify and remove hazardous substances. Dismantle components of products such as appliances.

Occupation Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Description: The "53-1000 Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers" category includes occupations that involve the supervision of the transportation of goods and people, as well as the movement of materials within warehouses, storage yards, or construction sites.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Description: Coordinate and supervise workers who load and unload aircraft cargo. Oversee cargo handling equipment, verify load weights, and ensure compliance with flight safety procedures.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of ground crew in the loading, unloading, securing, and staging of aircraft cargo or baggage. May determine the quantity and orientation of cargo and compute aircraft center of gravity. May accompany aircraft as member of flight crew and monitor and handle cargo in flight, and assist and brief passengers on safety and emergency procedures. Includes loadmasters.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Description: Direct and coordinate the activities of workers who move freight or stock by hand. Assign tasks, schedule shifts, and enforce safety protocols.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate the activities of helpers, laborers, or material movers.

Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Helpers, Laborers, and Material Movers, Hand
Description: Supervise curbside and drop-off recycling programs for municipal governments or private firms.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Transportation and Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Description: Supervise and schedule machine or vehicle operators (e.g., crane, forklift, or truck drivers). Ensure correct loading, adherence to regulations, and on-time deliveries.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Transportation and Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
Minor Name: Supervisors of Transportation and Material Moving Workers
Broad Name: First-Line Supervisors of Transportation and Material-Moving Machine and Vehicle Operators
Description: Directly supervise and coordinate activities of transportation and material-moving machine and vehicle operators and helpers.

The "53-2000 Air Transportation Workers" category encompasses a variety of occupations that deal with the operation and facilitation of air travel. This includes jobs such as pilots, flight attendants, and air traffic controllers, among others. Workers in this field typically require specialized training and certification due to the high level of responsibility and the technical knowledge required.

The "53-3000 Motor Vehicle Operators" category includes a range of occupations involving the operation of motor vehicles to transport people and goods. This category includes jobs such as bus drivers, taxi drivers, truck drivers, ambulance drivers, and more. Each of these jobs requires specific skills, certifications, and knowledge about safety regulations.
Fly and navigate airplanes or helicopters. Monitor instruments, communicate with air traffic control, and ensure passenger and aircraft safety.

Occupation Name: Airline Pilots, Copilots, and Flight Engineers
Description: Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-wing, multi-engine aircraft, usually on scheduled air carrier routes, for the transport of passengers and cargo. Requires Federal Air Transport Pilot certificate and rating for specific aircraft type used. Includes regional, National, and international airline pilots and flight instructors of airline pilots.

Pilot and navigate the flight of fixed-winged aircraft on nonscheduled air carrier routes, or helicopters. Requires Commercial Pilot certificate. Includes charter pilots with similar certification, and air ambulance and air tour pilots.

Occupation Name: Air Traffic Controllers and Airfield Operations Specialists
Description: Coordinate safe takeoffs and landings of aircraft. Issue landing and takeoff instructions, manage runway traffic, and ensure minimal risks at airports.

Broad Name: Air Traffic Controllers and Airfield Operations Specialists
Description: Control air traffic on and within vicinity of airport and movement of air traffic between altitude sectors and control centers according to established procedures and policies. Authorize, regulate, and control commercial airline flights according to government or company regulations to expedite and ensure flight safety.

Broad Name: Air Traffic Controllers and Airfield Operations Specialists
Description: Ensure the safe takeoff and landing of commercial and military aircraft. Duties include coordination between air-traffic control and maintenance personnel; dispatching; using airfield landing and navigational aids; implementing airfield safety procedures; monitoring and maintaining flight records; and applying knowledge of weather information.
Provide personal services to ensure the safety and comfort of airline passengers. Demonstrate emergency equipment usage, serve refreshments, and respond to passenger requests.

Provide personal services to ensure the safety, security, and comfort of airline passengers during flight. Greet passengers, verify tickets, explain use of safety equipment, and serve food or beverages.

Occupation Name: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
Description: Drive ambulances to transport sick or injured persons. Follow instructions from dispatchers, assist paramedics as needed, and ensure safe transport to medical facilities.

Occupation Name: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
Broad Name: Ambulance Drivers and Attendants, Except Emergency Medical Technicians
Description: Drive ambulance or assist ambulance driver in transporting sick, injured, or convalescent persons. Assist in lifting patients.
Operate buses to transport passengers along scheduled routes or on chartered trips. Maintain schedules, collect fares, and comply with traffic laws and safety regulations.
Drive bus or motor coach, including regular route operations, charters, and private carriage. May assist passengers with baggage. May collect fares or tickets.

Occupation Name: Bus Drivers, School or Special Client
Description: Transport students or special clients, such as the elderly or persons with disabilities. Ensure adherence to safety rules. May assist passengers in boarding or exiting.
Transport goods or passengers, often operating large trucks or delivery vehicles. May also handle sales, load/unload cargo, track inventory, and ensure accurate deliveries.

Drive truck or other vehicle over established routes or within an established territory and sell or deliver goods, such as food products, including restaurant take-out items, or pick up or deliver items such as commercial laundry. May also take orders, collect payment, or stock merchandise at point of delivery. Includes newspaper delivery drivers.
Drive a tractor-trailer combination or a truck with a capacity of at least 26,000 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW). May be required to unload truck. Requires commercial drivers' license.

Occupation Name: Light Truck or Delivery Services Drivers
Description: Drive a light vehicle, such as a truck or van, with a capacity of less than 26,000 pounds Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), primarily to deliver or pick up merchandise or to deliver packages. May load and unload vehicle.
Drive automobiles or limousines to transport passengers. Collect fares, assist with luggage, and follow local driving regulations.
Drive automobiles, vans, or limousines to transport passengers. May occasionally carry cargo. Includes hearse drivers.
Operate specialized motor vehicles, not included under other standard driver categories, possibly including shuttle or vehicle test drivers.
All motor vehicle operators not listed separately.

The "53-4000 Rail Transportation Workers" category includes occupations that involve the operation and maintenance of trains and rail systems. This includes roles such as locomotive engineers, conductors, and yardmasters, among others. These workers ensure the safe and efficient transportation of passengers and goods via rail systems.
Drive locomotives to transport passengers or freight. Monitor instruments, interpret signals, and oversee safe train operation.

Drive electric, diesel-electric, steam, or gas-turbine-electric locomotives to transport passengers or freight. Interpret train orders, electronic or manual signals, and railroad rules and regulations.

Monitor locomotive instruments and watch for dragging equipment, obstacles on rights-of-way, and train signals during run. Watch for and relay traffic signals from yard workers to yard engineer in railroad yard.

Occupation Name: Rail Yard Engineers, Dinkey Operators, and Hostlers
Description: Drive switching or other locomotive or dinkey engines within railroad yard, industrial plant, quarry, construction project, or similar location.

Occupation Name: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators
Description: Operate track switches, couple or uncouple cars, or assist in controlling train movement. Monitor signals, follow dispatchers’ instructions, and maintain safety.

Occupation Name: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators
Broad Name: Railroad Brake, Signal, and Switch Operators
Description: Operate railroad track switches. Couple or uncouple rolling stock to make up or break up trains. Signal engineers by hand or flagging. May inspect couplings, air hoses, journal boxes, and hand brakes.
Coordinate train crew activities, manage railcars, and operate within rail yards to ensure safe train assembly and movement.

Coordinate activities of switch-engine crew within railroad yard, industrial plant, or similar location. Conductors coordinate activities of train crew on passenger or freight trains. Yardmasters review train schedules and switching orders and coordinate activities of workers engaged in railroad traffic operations, such as the makeup or breakup of trains and yard switching.
Drive electric-powered streetcars or subways. Follow schedules, stop at designated stations, operate doors, and ensure passenger safety.
Operate subway or elevated suburban trains with no separate locomotive, or electric-powered streetcar, to transport passengers. May handle fares.
Perform tasks in rail transportation not covered by other job titles. Might include specialized signaling, track inspection, or passenger assistance roles.
All rail transportation workers not listed separately.

The "53-5000 Water Transportation Workers" category encompasses occupations that involve the operation and maintenance of vessels that transport passengers and cargo over water. This includes roles such as ship captains, mates, sailors, marine oilers, and ship engineers. These workers are responsible for managing the vessel, ensuring the safety of passengers and cargo, and maintaining the ship's equipment and structures.
Stand watch, handle lines, or maintain decks on ships or other water vessels. Lubricate machinery, repair cables, and manage onboard tasks for efficient operation.

Stand watch to look for obstructions in path of vessel, measure water depth, turn wheel on bridge, or use emergency equipment as directed by captain, mate, or pilot. Break out, rig, overhaul, and store cargo-handling gear, stationary rigging, and running gear. Perform a variety of maintenance tasks to preserve the painted surface of the ship and to maintain line and ship equipment. Must hold government-issued certification and tankerman certification when working aboard liquid-carrying vessels. Includes able seamen and ordinary seamen.

Occupation Name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
Description: Command water vessels like tugboats, ferries, or cargo ships. Navigate routes, supervise crew, and ensure safe loading and unloading of cargo or passengers.

Occupation Name: Captains, Mates, and Pilots of Water Vessels
Broad Name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
Description: Command or supervise operations of ships and water vessels, such as tugboats and ferryboats. Required to hold license issued by U.S. Coast Guard.

Broad Name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
Description: Command vessels in oceans, bays, lakes, rivers, or coastal waters.

Broad Name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
Description: Supervise or coordinate activities of crew aboard ships, boats, barges, or dredges.

Broad Name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
Description: Command ships to steer them into and out of harbors, estuaries, straits, or sounds, or on rivers, lakes, or bays. Must be licensed by U.S. Coast Guard with limitations indicating class and tonnage of vessels for which license is valid and route and waters that may be piloted.

Broad Name: Ship and Boat Captains and Operators
Description: Operate small motor-driven boats. May assist in navigational activities.
Operate and maintain engines and related systems aboard ships. Monitor machinery, troubleshoot issues, and oversee repairs to ensure vessel safety.
Supervise and coordinate activities of crew engaged in operating and maintaining engines, boilers, deck machinery, and electrical, sanitary, and refrigeration equipment aboard ship.

The "53-6000 Other Transportation Workers" category includes a variety of occupations that involve transportation services not classified in other categories. This includes roles such as parking lot attendants, automotive and watercraft service attendants, transportation inspectors, freight and cargo inspectors, and bridge and lock tenders.
Operate and monitor drawbridges, locks, or similar mechanisms to allow boat traffic. Communicate with vessel operators and manage signals or gates.

Operate and tend bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses to permit marine passage on inland waterways, near shores, and at danger points in waterway passages. May supervise such operations. Includes drawbridge operators, lock operators, and slip bridge operators.
Park or retrieve vehicles for customers at parking facilities. Collect fees, provide directions, and maintain orderly traffic flow.
Park vehicles or issue tickets for customers in a parking lot or garage. May collect fee.
Provide fueling, cleaning, or routine maintenance for cars or boats. May check fluid levels, wash vehicles, and offer basic customer service.

Service automobiles, buses, trucks, boats, and other automotive or marine vehicles with fuel, lubricants, and accessories. Collect payment for services and supplies. May lubricate vehicle, change motor oil, install antifreeze, or replace lights or other accessories, such as windshield wiper blades or fan belts. May repair or replace tires.
Collect and analyze traffic data, set up traffic counters, evaluate patterns, and suggest traffic flow improvements.
Conduct field studies to determine traffic volume, speed, effectiveness of signals, adequacy of lighting, and other factors influencing traffic conditions, under direction of traffic engineer.
Examine transportation equipment (aircraft, ships, or railcars) to ensure compliance with regulations. Check safety devices, review documentation, and investigate accidents.

Inspect equipment or goods in connection with the safe transport of cargo or people. Includes rail transportation inspectors, such as freight inspectors; rail inspectors; and other inspectors of transportation vehicles, not elsewhere classified.
Inspect aircraft, maintenance procedures, air navigational aids, air traffic controls, and communications equipment to ensure conformance with Federal safety regulations.

Occupation Name: Transportation Vehicle, Equipment and Systems Inspectors, Except Aviation
Description: Inspect and monitor transportation equipment, vehicles, or systems to ensure compliance with regulations and safety standards.
Inspect the handling, storage, and stowing of freight and cargoes.
Provide services to ensure passenger comfort or safety on trains, ships, or buses. Greet passengers, check tickets, and offer basic assistance.

Provide services to ensure the safety and comfort of passengers aboard ships, buses, trains, or within the station or terminal. Perform duties such as greeting passengers, explaining the use of safety equipment, serving meals or beverages, or answering questions related to travel.
Occupations in transportation support not classified elsewhere. May include auto transporters, people who pilot specialized vehicles, or traffic escorts.
All transportation workers not listed separately.

The "53-7000 Material Moving Workers" category covers occupations that involve moving freight, stock, or other materials or helping others to move materials. This includes roles such as conveyor operators, crane and tower operators, dredge operators, hoist and winch operators, industrial truck and tractor operators, cleaners of vehicles and equipment, laborers and freight, stock, and material movers, hand packers, and packagers.
Control conveyor systems to move materials or products. Adjust speeds, distribute loads, and clear jams to maintain safe, efficient flow.

Control or tend conveyors or conveyor systems that move materials or products to and from stockpiles, processing stations, departments, or vehicles. May control speed and routing of materials or products.
Operate mechanical cranes or towers to lift, move, and position loads. Calculate load weights, follow signals, and monitor equipment performance.
Operate mechanical boom and cable or tower and cable equipment to lift and move materials, machines, or products in many directions.

Occupation Name: Dredge, Excavating, and Loading Machine Operators
Description: Use machinery to scoop or scrape earth, sand, gravel, or other materials. Dredge waterways or load trucks in construction or mining.

Broad Name: Dredge, Excavating, and Loading Machine Operators
Description: Operate dredge to remove sand, gravel, or other materials in order to excavate and maintain navigable channels in waterways.

Occupation Name: Excavating and Loading Machine and Dragline Operators
Broad Name: Dredge, Excavating, and Loading Machine Operators
Description: Operate or tend machinery equipped with scoops, shovels, or buckets, to excavate and load loose materials.

Broad Name: Dredge, Excavating, and Loading Machine Operators
Description: Operate underground loading machine to load coal, ore, or rock into shuttle or mine car or onto conveyors. Loading equipment may include power shovels, hoisting engines equipped with cable-drawn scraper or scoop, or machines equipped with gathering arms and conveyor.
Operate hoists or winches to move loads vertically. Work with riggers or crane operators, follow signals, and keep logs of materials moved.
Operate or tend hoists or winches to lift and pull loads using power-operated cable equipment.
Drive industrial trucks or tractors equipped with forklifts, booms, or other devices to move materials in warehouses or construction sites.
Operate industrial trucks or tractors equipped to move materials around a warehouse, storage yard, factory, construction site, or similar location.
Manually move freight, stock, or other materials. May load or unload trucks, carry items, or sort shipments in warehouses or production facilities.
Wash or otherwise clean vehicles, machinery, and other equipment. Use such materials as water, cleaning agents, brushes, cloths, and hoses.

Occupation Name: Laborers and Freight, Stock, and Material Movers, Hand
Description: Manually move freight, stock, or other materials or perform other general labor. Includes all manual laborers not elsewhere classified.
Feed materials into or remove materials from machines or equipment that is automatic or tended by other workers.
Pack or package by hand a wide variety of products and materials.
Tend and maintain pumps for transferring materials like oil, gas, or water. Monitor pressure gauges, regulate flow, and perform routine maintenance.

Occupation Name: Gas Compressor and Gas Pumping Station Operators
Description: Operate steam, gas, electric motor, or internal combustion engine driven compressors. Transmit, compress, or recover gases, such as butane, nitrogen, hydrogen, and natural gas.

Tend, control, or operate power-driven, stationary, or portable pumps and manifold systems to transfer gases, oil, other liquids, slurries, or powdered materials to and from various vessels and processes.
Operate power pumps and auxiliary equipment to produce flow of oil or gas from wells in oil field.
Collect and transport garbage or recyclable materials from homes and businesses. Operate trucks or equipment, follow routes, and ensure safe disposal.
Collect and dump refuse or recyclable materials from containers into truck. May drive truck.
Operate diesel or electric-powered shuttle cars in underground mines to transport coal or ore. Maneuver in tight spaces and maintain safety.
Operate diesel or electric-powered shuttle car in underground mine to transport materials from working face to mine cars or conveyor.

Occupation Name: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
Description: Load and unload chemicals or bulk solids into or from tank cars, trucks, or ships. Use pumps, hoses, or conveyor belts and adhere to safety and environmental rules.

Occupation Name: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
Broad Name: Tank Car, Truck, and Ship Loaders
Description: Load and unload chemicals and bulk solids, such as coal, sand, and grain into or from tank cars, trucks, or ships using material moving equipment. May perform a variety of other tasks relating to shipment of products. May gauge or sample shipping tanks and test them for leaks.
Conduct specialized material-moving duties not included in other categories, such as rigging, logging yard operations, or forklift duties in unique settings.
All material moving workers not listed separately.

Encompasses all roles specific to the armed forces, including enlisted and officer positions. Individuals in these occupations perform national defense duties, from combat operations to specialized tactical support.

Occupation Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: The "55-1000 Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders" category includes roles focused on leading operations and units in the U.S. Armed Forces. These include high-level leaders in special operations, such as those within the Army Special Forces, Navy SEALs, Air Force Special Operations, Marine Corps Special Operations, and other similar groups. It's important to note that military pay is not determined in the same way as civilian pay. It's primarily based on rank and years of service, and it includes allowances for housing, food, and other benefits.

Occupation Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Lead units in specialized military operations (infantry, special forces, or tactical teams). Plan missions, oversee personnel, coordinate logistics, and manage training.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Perform and direct in-flight duties to ensure the successful completion of combat, reconnaissance, transport, and search and rescue missions. Duties include operating aircraft communications and radar equipment, such as establishing satellite linkages and jamming enemy communications capabilities; operating aircraft weapons and defensive systems; conducting pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight inspections of onboard equipment; and directing cargo and personnel drops.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Plan and direct the operation and maintenance of catapults, arresting gear, and associated mechanical, hydraulic, and control systems involved primarily in aircraft carrier takeoff and landing operations. Duties include supervision of readiness and safety of arresting gear, launching equipment, barricades, and visual landing aid systems; planning and coordinating the design, development, and testing of launch and recovery systems; preparing specifications for catapult and arresting gear installations; evaluating design proposals; determining handling equipment needed for new aircraft; preparing technical data and instructions for operation of landing aids; and training personnel in carrier takeoff and landing procedures.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Direct the operation of tanks, light armor, and amphibious assault vehicle units during combat situations on land or in aquatic environments. Duties include directing crew members in the operation of targeting and firing systems; coordinating the operation of advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment; directing the transport of personnel and equipment during combat; formulating and implementing battle plans, including the tactical employment of armored vehicle units; and coordinating with infantry, artillery, and air support units.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Manage personnel and weapons operations to destroy enemy positions, aircraft, and vessels. Duties include planning, targeting, and coordinating the tactical deployment of field artillery and air defense artillery missile systems units; directing the establishment and operation of fire control communications systems; targeting and launching intercontinental ballistic missiles; directing the storage and handling of nuclear munitions and components; overseeing security of weapons storage and launch facilities; and managing maintenance of weapons systems.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Manage the operation of communications, detection, and weapons systems essential for controlling air, ground, and naval operations. Duties include managing critical communication links between air, naval, and ground forces; formulating and implementing emergency plans for natural and wartime disasters; coordinating emergency response teams and agencies; evaluating command center information and need for high-level military and government reporting; managing the operation of surveillance and detection systems; providing technical information and advice on capabilities and operational readiness; and directing operation of weapons targeting, firing, and launch computer systems.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Direct, train, and lead infantry units in ground combat operations. Duties include directing deployment of infantry weapons, vehicles, and equipment; directing location, construction, and camouflage of infantry positions and equipment; managing field communications operations; coordinating with armor, artillery, and air support units; performing strategic and tactical planning, including battle plan development; and leading basic reconnaissance operations.

Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: Lead elite teams that implement unconventional operations by air, land, or sea during combat or peacetime. These activities include offensive raids, demolitions, reconnaissance, search and rescue, and counterterrorism. In addition to their combat training, special forces officers often have specialized training in swimming, diving, parachuting, survival, emergency medicine, and foreign languages. Duties include directing advanced reconnaissance operations and evaluating intelligence information; recruiting, training, and equipping friendly forces; leading raids and invasions on enemy territories; training personnel to implement individual missions and contingency plans; performing strategic and tactical planning for politically sensitive missions; and operating sophisticated communications equipment.

Occupation Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders, All Other
Minor Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Broad Name: Military Officer Special and Tactical Operations Leaders
Description: All military officer special and tactical operations leaders not listed separately.

The "55-2000 First-Line Enlisted Military Supervisors" category includes roles that primarily involve leading and coordinating the activities of enlisted military personnel. These roles typically involve supervision of enlisted personnel and may include roles such as squad leaders, section leaders, flight line chiefs, and others.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of enlisted personnel. Provide leadership, training, and administrative support for teams within various branches of the armed forces.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Air Crew Members
Description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of air crew members. Supervisors may also perform the same activities as the workers they supervise.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of Weapons Specialists/Crew Members
Description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of weapons specialists/crew members. Supervisors may also perform the same activities as the workers they supervise.

Occupation Name: First-Line Supervisors of All Other Tactical Operations Specialists
Description: Supervise and coordinate the activities of all other tactical operations specialists not classified separately above. Supervisors may also perform the same activities as the workers they supervise.

Occupation Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: The "55-3000 Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members" category includes roles that involve technical and tactical operations in the U.S. Armed Forces. These roles typically require specialized training and skills and may include roles such as infantry, artillery specialists, combat vehicle crew, aircraft weapons specialists, and others.

Occupation Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Operate, maintain, and monitor weapons or aircraft systems, often in combat or tactical missions. Provide direct support to ground, air, or naval units.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Perform in-flight duties to ensure the successful completion of combat, reconnaissance, transport, and search and rescue missions. Duties include operating aircraft communications and detection equipment, including establishing satellite linkages and jamming enemy communications capabilities; conducting pre-flight, in-flight, and post-flight inspections of onboard equipment; operating and maintaining aircraft weapons and defensive systems; operating and maintaining aircraft in-flight refueling systems; executing aircraft safety and emergency procedures; computing and verifying passenger, cargo, fuel, and emergency and special equipment weight and balance data; and conducting cargo and personnel drops.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Operate and maintain catapults, arresting gear, and associated mechanical, hydraulic, and control systems involved primarily in aircraft carrier takeoff and landing operations. Duties include installing and maintaining visual landing aids; testing and maintaining launch and recovery equipment using electric and mechanical test equipment and hand tools; activating airfield arresting systems, such as crash barriers and cables, during emergency landing situations; directing aircraft launch and recovery operations using hand or light signals; and maintaining logs of airplane launches, recoveries, and equipment maintenance.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Operate tanks, light armor, and amphibious assault vehicles during combat situations on land or in aquatic environments. Duties include driving armored vehicles which require specialized training; operating and maintaining targeting and firing systems; operating and maintaining advanced onboard communications and navigation equipment; transporting personnel and equipment in a combat environment; and operating and maintaining auxiliary weapons, including machine guns and grenade launchers.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Target, fire, and maintain weapons used to destroy enemy positions, aircraft, and vessels. Field artillery crew members predominantly use guns, cannons, and howitzers in ground combat operations, while air defense artillery crew members predominantly use missiles and rockets. Naval artillery crew members predominantly use torpedoes and missiles launched from a ship or submarine. Duties include testing, inspecting, and storing ammunition, missiles, and torpedoes; conducting preventive and routine maintenance on weapons and related equipment; establishing and maintaining radio and wire communications; and operating weapons targeting, firing, and launch computer systems.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Operate and monitor communications, detection, and weapons systems essential for controlling air, ground, and naval operations. Duties include maintaining and relaying critical communications between air, naval, and ground forces; implementing emergency plans for natural and wartime disasters; relaying command center information to high-level military and government decision makers; monitoring surveillance and detection systems, such as air defense; interpreting and evaluating tactical situations and making recommendations to superiors; and operating weapons targeting, firing, and launch computer systems.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Operate weapons and equipment in ground combat operations. Duties include operating and maintaining weapons, such as rifles, machine guns, mortars, and hand grenades; locating, constructing, and camouflaging infantry positions and equipment; evaluating terrain and recording topographical information; operating and maintaining field communications equipment; assessing need for and directing supporting fire; placing explosives and performing minesweeping activities on land; and participating in basic reconnaissance operations.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Operate equipment using radio or sound wave technology to identify, track, and analyze objects or natural phenomena of military interest. Includes airborne, shipboard, and terrestrial positions. May perform minor maintenance.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Implement unconventional operations by air, land, or sea during combat or peacetime as members of elite teams. These activities include offensive raids, demolitions, reconnaissance, search and rescue, and counterterrorism. In addition to their combat training, special forces members often have specialized training in swimming, diving, parachuting, survival, emergency medicine, and foreign languages. Duties include conducting advanced reconnaissance operations and collecting intelligence information; recruiting, training, and equipping friendly forces; conducting raids and invasions on enemy territories; laying and detonating explosives for demolition targets; locating, identifying, defusing, and disposing of ordnance; and operating and maintaining sophisticated communications equipment.

Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: Implement unconventional operations by air, land, or sea during combat or peacetime as members of elite teams. These activities include offensive raids, demolitions, reconnaissance, search and rescue, and counterterrorism. In addition to their combat training, special forces members often have specialized training in swimming, diving, parachuting, survival, emergency medicine, and foreign languages. Duties include conducting advanced reconnaissance operations and collecting intelligence information; recruiting, training, and equipping friendly forces; conducting raids and invasions on enemy territories; laying and detonating explosives for demolition targets; locating, identifying, defusing, and disposing of ordnance; and operating and maintaining sophisticated communications equipment.

Occupation Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members, All Other
Minor Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Broad Name: Military Enlisted Tactical Operations and Air/Weapons Specialists and Crew Members
Description: All military enlisted tactical operations and air/weapons specialists and crew members not listed separately.
